title: M0 — the real slice: substrate + exemplar skill + Tier-0 verifier + tier gate (40-bit toy curve end to end)
description:
WHY THIS MILESTONE EXISTS
Cairn is a research harness whose epistemics are immutable and whose strategy is mutable (PLAN §0; CLAUDE.md). M0 builds the one vertical slice everything else plugs into: a content-addressed substrate (SQLite + BLAKE3), one exemplar skill built end to end (content-addressed I/O, captured seed, known-answer self-test, declared cost profile), the Tier-0 verifier (`xP == Q` in a subprocess), and the tier gate with its gate bundle + pin. "Everything else plugs into this shape — get it right once, the verifier included." Build M0 before adding another design layer: a running 40-bit slice reveals more than more architecture.

OPERATOR DECISIONS THAT BIND M0 (confirmed 2026-08-21; recorded in PLAN §16)
(1) PARI-only arithmetic at M0 with the BSGS-vs-SEA *algorithm* cross-check through 50 bits; the gmpy2 Hasse-interval BSGS enters as the *implementation* axis at M1.
(2) One 60-bit rho measured with cypari2 at M0 (bead m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15); a compiled baseline is funded at M1 only if the interpreted rung cannot finish inside the Tier-1 budget.
(5) Skill yanks and `salt` issuance are human-only, like waivers — at M0 the `yank_records`/`salts` rows therefore carry the human-path digest+offset columns (schema only; behavior M1).
(8) No separate OS user for the orchestrator before M3; at M0 the gate-bundle pin and the attestation file are protected by file mode/flags only, and the grounding brief records exactly what that does and does not refuse (probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6/APFS: mode 0644 + `uappnd` lets the owner append and refuses overwrite, `r+`, truncate AND `chmod` while the flag stands; 0444 + `uappnd` refuses append too, so the attestation file is 0644+uappnd and the pin is 0444+uappnd; the owner can still `chflags nouappnd` — the one-user gap).
(9) A ticket carries its gate-bundle hash; a mismatch re-mints the ticket.

STACK FACTS M0 STANDS ON (probed on this Mac 2026-08-21; research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md)
PARI/GP 2.17.4 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gp (the shell has `alias gp='git push'` — always use the full path); cypari2 2.2.4 bundles libpari 2.17.2 and produced bit-identical p,a,b,n,tries to gp for the toy-curve search; `ellcard` is milliseconds through 50 bits, ≈75 ms/curve at 60 bits and overflows the default 8 MB PARI stack (use `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000)` / `gp -s 64M`); gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow) with the message on stderr, zero-fills missing arguments, and writes nothing to stderr on a successful quiet run (so the verifier's empty-stderr accept predicate is satisfiable); the PARI PRNG state is advanced by `ellsea(E)` and by 60-bit `ellcard`/`ellsea(E,1)` but not by ≤ 50-bit `ellcard`, so `toy_curve` pins its call sequence (cairn-m0-e0s.6); under SQLite's rollback journal only `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` blocks a reader (the WAL probe's control arm, cairn-m0-e0s.2); Sage absent; elan/lean absent; gp's own startup needs more than 2 MB of PARI stack (`gp -q -f -s 2M` exits 1 at startup with `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout and the overflow message on stderr) while `verify.gp` on the 60-bit instance prints OK at every ceiling ≥ 3M including the 8 MB default because `verify()` never calls `ellcard` — so the verifier's forced-crash fixture is the bundle script's `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` entry (a 60-bit `ellcard` under `8M`: rc 0, empty stdout, overflow on stderr; cairn-m0-e0s.8/.11), never `verify()` at 8M; a file carrying `uappnd` cannot be unlinked or renamed by its owner while the flag stands (EPERM), so every test that flags a file under tmp_path clears the flag in teardown; CPython's `Popen.communicate()` reaps the child through `wait()`, so the runner captures stdout/stderr to files and reaps with `os.wait4` alone (cairn-m0-e0s.9). M0 re-executes the facts it relies on as tests and records the rest (WAL, busy timeout, append-only flag, write boundary) — bead m0-grounding-probes (cairn-m0-e0s.2).

DONE WHEN (PLAN §13 M0):
- the exemplar skill `toy_curve(bits, seed)` runs on a 40-bit toy curve; a deterministic M0 fixture (an integration fixture, not a second research skill) derives `x` and `Q = xP` from that output; the subprocess verifier accepts that pair, rejects a one-coordinate and a one-scalar negative fixture, classifies a forced backend crash as FAIL, and refuses — before the subprocess spawns — a submission that names its own `(P, Q)` rather than the statement node's;
- the generator output, derivation receipt, verifier result and gate-run record are hashed, self-tested, cost-tagged substrate nodes;
- the tier gate refuses a fixture launch declaring a tier two above its ticket and records `TierRefused`; a gate run against a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed;
- a write to the pin and a write to the attestation file, each attempted as the orchestrator's process user, are refused by the operating system, and a `review_verdict` row whose digest matches no attestation record is absent to `justify`;
- `justify` returns STRONG-EMPIRICAL from a synthetic `ladder_table` evidence node with verdict KEEP whose attempt carries a passed reproducibility record, returns the CONJECTURE ceiling for the same table with that record absent or its grade `AuditOnly`, returns a coverage violation when the table's population does not cover the statement's scope, and returns a lattice violation when a synthetic `statistical` node is offered for PROVEN, against a synthetic statement hash;
- a blob unreachable from the roots table is collectable while a rooted one is not;
- the first gate self-tests run before the gates: the verifier's planted `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures and the canonicalizer's known-answer vectors for both keys.

SCHEMA-ONLY AT M0 (behavior exercised at M1): escrow reserve/spend/release, yank reach and `disowned` propagation, and the process-tree form of the budget ceiling — M0's runner already enforces the ceiling on the direct child's wall clock (4× the declared expectation, status `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, cairn-m0-e0s.9). M0 has a fixture writing and reading each such column. A behavior no M0 test exercises is architecture, not a slice.

ENGINEERING RULES FOR EVERY CHILD BEAD
- Integration test first (real PARI via cypari2, real gp subprocess, real SQLite file), unit tests second: unit tests cover the pure predicates (canonical encoding, the verifier's pre-spawn validator and accept predicate, the tier-gate predicate, `justify`'s coverage comparator and kind→class map, the runner's status mapping); e2e is `tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py`. No mock may stand in for the gate under test; a planted fault (a monkeypatched backend answer, a killed child) is not a mock of the gate.
- Logging: one logger (`src/cairn/log.py`, bead cairn-m0-e0s.1) used by every CLI and every gate decision; each record names the step, the input hashes, the `gate_runs` row id where one exists, the verdict with its reasons and the timing; `--log DEBUG` (or `CAIRN_LOG=DEBUG`) adds subprocess argv and stdin/stdout/stderr digests; tests assert on the log records wherever a verdict is involved (pytest caplog), so a silent gate is a failing test.
- Python via `uv` only (`uv run pytest`, `uv add`); never bare pip/python; subprocesses use `sys.executable`.
- CLI convention (defined once in cairn-m0-e0s.1): every `cairn` subcommand takes the global options `--db` (default `var/substrate.sqlite`), `--bundle` (`deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`), `--pin` (`deploy/gate-bundle.pin`), `--attest` (`deploy/attestations.log`) and `--log LEVEL`; no subcommand spells its own variant of these paths.
- Zero explanatory comments in code; names carry meaning.
- Every child carries a positive observable, a planted negative (a fixture that must FAIL), and a No-Claim line (what green does not prove).
- Closure of a child is a claim until its commands are re-executed at close; paste command + output in the close comment. The epic closes only when `uv run pytest` is green on a fresh clone and `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` (bead m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14) produces the four nodes.

SHARED FIXTURES (named once, used by several beads): `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` — the 60-bit (p,a,b,n,P) that the grounding brief's bench.gp yields at bits=60 seed=1, generated once with gp and committed by cairn-m0-e0s.1; the stack-fact test (.1), the verifier's 60-bit and forced-crash tests (.8), the gate plan's crash fixture (.11) read it, and cairn-m0-e0s.6 asserts `toy_curve(60, 1)` reproduces it. `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` — one brief with sections written by .2 (stack facts), .6 (tries table), .15 (rho at 60 bits).

NOT IN M0: the ladder, baseline skills, Lean gate, workers, orchestrator, parallel tracks (M1–M4 epics). The research tree is never pre-decomposed into beads (CLAUDE.md).

TEST PLAN (shapes) — ENGINEERING RULES ADDED FOR EVERY CHILD BEAD
- Layer discipline: pure functions are unit tests in `tests/unit/` (the canon encoder/decoder, the coverage comparator, the accept-predicate truth table, the tier-gate predicate, the runner's status mapping, gate-plan validation, GC reachability); anything touching gp, SQLite, PARI, file modes/flags or a subprocess is integration in `tests/integration/`; `cairn m0-run` is e2e in `tests/e2e/`. Pure modules are pyramid-shaped (unit-dominant); gate/CLI modules are trophy-shaped (integration-dominant).
- No fake-unit tests: a unit test that monkeypatches three or more boundaries is an integration test in disguise — promote it to `tests/integration/` against the real components or delete it.
- Parametrize failure paths instead of duplicating tests: every refusal/violation/trigger table is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over (input, expected reason) with `match=` on every raise; two tests differing only in data are merged.
- No cross-layer redundancy: each known-answer vector is asserted exactly once, in unit (`tests/unit/test_canon.py`, `tests/unit/test_claims_kat.py`); integration and e2e tests assert behavior, never re-assert KAT values.
- Before closing a child, run `/optimal-tests --audit <its test files>` and act on every finding; the audit's triage table is pasted in the close comment beside the test output.
- Structured test logging: `tests/conftest.py` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) installs an autouse `json_test_log` fixture that routes `src/cairn/log.py` records to `tmp_path/test.log.jsonl` as JSON lines `{ts, test, phase: setup|act|assert|teardown, step, ids/hashes, verdict, wall_ms}` plus a `db_snapshot(substrate, label)` helper writing `{event:'db_snapshot', label, counts:{table: n}}`; the file is attached to the pytest report on failure; every integration test that touches the substrate calls `db_snapshot` at least once after its act phase.
- Factories: `tests/factories.py` (cairn-m0-e0s.5) holds realistic synthetic builders — `claim_statement(family, size, assumptions, cost_model)`, `hypothesis_object(...)`, `evidence_node(kind, target, population, assumptions, verdict, repro)`, `ladder_table_keep(...)`, `repro_record(passed)`, `review_verdict(...)`, `selftest_summary(origins, arm, cross_check)`, `instance_from_vector()` — producing canon-valid objects with a per-test seed; used by cairn-m0-e0s.5, .10, .12 (and the synthetic statement node of .14); tests never hand-roll these dicts.
- Isolation: every test runs under tmp_path only; `tests/conftest.py` autouse `isolation_guard` fixture snapshots the repo's `deploy/` and `var/` trees (paths, sizes, mtimes) before and after each test and fails the test on any delta; it wraps `subprocess.Popen` with a spy (not a mock — the real Popen is called) that fails the test if `argv[0]` is anything but `sys.executable` or `cairn.pari.GP_BIN`; it scrubs `CAIRN_DB*` from `os.environ` for the test's duration.
- Mock policy: `monkeypatch` is allowed only as declared fault injection inside a skill's own seam — the `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrapper returning n+2 (cairn-m0-e0s.6), a fixture skill that exits 3 or sleeps (cairn-m0-e0s.9), a missing `GP_BIN` path (cairn-m0-e0s.1) — never as a stand-in for gp, SQLite, PARI, the bundle, the pin, the attestation file or any gate under test; a spy that calls through and records is not a mock; `tests/unit/test_no_mocks_in_integration.py` greps `tests/integration/` and `tests/e2e/` for `unittest.mock`/`MagicMock`/`mocker.patch` and fails on any hit.
- Property-based and fuzz tests use Hypothesis only (dev dependency, profiles pinned in `tests/conftest.py`, cairn-m0-e0s.1; atheris does not build on this Mac — probed 2026-08-21, its wheel needs a custom libFuzzer clang — so it is omitted); every metamorphic relation names the planted mutant it kills in `tests/mutants/<module>_mutants.py`, and a relation that kills no mutant is deleted; every fuzz target has a seed corpus under `tests/fuzz_corpus/<target>/` holding the bead's planted negatives, replayed as `@example`s before random generation, with ≥ 500 examples per target under the `ci` profile.
- Goldens: known-answer vectors and committed curve rows live under `tests/vectors/`; frozen transcripts, certificate values and the bundle hash under `tests/goldens/`; `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` records, per golden, the generator command, tool versions and a volatility note (canon/claims KATs and the bundle hash are deterministic and platform-independent; the CURVE60 vector, the toy-curve rows and the environment manifest depend on libpari/platform); `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest` regenerates, anything else fails on a difference with a unified diff, `*.actual` is gitignored, and a regenerated golden lands only in an attributed commit naming the reason — for the self-test floor and certificate (cairn-m0-e0s.7) this is PLAN §2's rule that only an attributed update may raise the floor or re-mint the certificate.
acceptance_criteria:
- All child beads closed with their own evidence re-executed at close.
- `uv run pytest` green on a fresh clone (integration + unit); output attached to the close comment.
- `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` writes four nodes (generator output, derivation receipt, verifier result, gate-run record) with content hashes, self-test references and cost tags; re-running with the same seed reproduces the generator output hash (Replayable).
- Every done-when bullet maps to a named test that was run, with command and output in the close comment.
- Planted negative (epic level): each planted fixture must fail or be refused — the verifier's `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures (cairn-m0-e0s.8/.11) and the gate plan's weakened-predicate and weakened-`verify.gp` bundle copies (.11), the tier-two-above launch (.10), the bundle whose hash ≠ pin (.10), the forged `review_verdict` digest (.10/.12), the uncertified revision (.7/.10/.14), the `statistical`-for-PROVEN offer (.12), the orphan blob that must be collectable while the rooted one survives (.13); any of these passing silently fails the epic.
- No-Claim: M0 green proves the slice's gates refuse the planted fixtures on this Mac; it proves nothing about ECDLP, about any research claim, or about behavior under a second OS user / Linux container.
- Engineering rules (test shapes) hold in every closed child: layer discipline (`tests/unit` pure, `tests/integration` gp/SQLite/PARI/flags, `tests/e2e` the slice), no fake-unit tests, parametrized failure tables, KATs asserted once in unit, `json_test_log` records and `db_snapshot` counts in every substrate-touching integration test, factories from `tests/factories.py` for every claim/hypothesis/evidence object, tmp_path-only isolation enforced by `isolation_guard`, monkeypatch only at a declared skill seam, `tests/unit/test_no_mocks_in_integration.py` green.
- Every metamorphic relation in the children names a killed mutant under `tests/mutants/`; every fuzz target has `tests/fuzz_corpus/<target>/` replayed as `@example`s and runs ≥ 500 Hypothesis examples under the `ci` profile; every golden has a PROVENANCE.md row with its volatility note and fails on drift without `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`; each child's close comment carries its `/optimal-tests --audit` triage table.
- The §2 skill-contract conformance harness (cairn-m0-e0s.16) passes toy_curve on every MUST clause and fails the planted non-conforming fixture on its named clauses before the epic closes.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.

title: M0: uv project scaffold + real-PARI smoke test (cypari2 in-process + gp subprocess + 60-bit stack fact)
description:
WHY: every later bead runs real PARI through two builds — cypari2 in-process for skills, /opt/homebrew/bin/gp as the verifier subprocess — and real SQLite. Nothing downstream is testable until the toolchain is pinned and a real call succeeds under `uv run`.

WHAT
- `uv init --package` layout: `pyproject.toml` (name `cairn`, Python ≥3.14 — cypari2 2.2.4 ships a 3.14 wheel per the grounding brief), `src/cairn/`, console script `cairn` (argparse is enough).
- Deps: `cypari2` (bundles libpari 2.17.2), `blake3`; dev: `pytest`. `gmpy2` is added at M1 only (operator decision 1).
- Dirs: `tests/integration/` (real PARI/gp/SQLite; the default suite), `tests/unit/`, `tests/e2e/`, `tests/vectors/`, `bundle/` (gate-bundle source), `deploy/` (built bundle + pin + attestation file; gitignored except a README), `var/` (runtime DBs; gitignored). `.gitignore`: `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `var/`, `deploy/*.sqlite`, `deploy/*.pin`, `deploy/*.log`.
- `src/cairn/pari.py`: one shared cypari2 handle; `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000, silent=True)` exactly once at import (the 60-bit `ellcard` overflows the 8 MB default — PROVEN by probe; `silent=True` keeps PARI's stack-size notice off the harness's stderr, as the grounding brief's `bench_cypari2.py` does); `GP_BIN = "/opt/homebrew/bin/gp"` with an existence check raising a typed error; `pari_versions()` returning `pari.version()` and the cypari2 version (they feed the environment-manifest digest in bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3); thin wrappers `ellcard(E)` / `ellsea(E, early_abort)` so a later test can plant a disagreement at one seam (cairn-m0-e0s.6). Never call gp through a shell.
- `src/cairn/cli.py`: argparse entry for the `cairn` console script; the global options `--db` (default `var/substrate.sqlite`), `--bundle` (`deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`), `--pin` (`deploy/gate-bundle.pin`), `--attest` (`deploy/attestations.log`) and `--log LEVEL` are defined once in a shared parent parser attached to the top-level parser and, through `parents=`, to every subparser — so `cairn --db X m0-run …` and `cairn m0-run … --db X` both parse to one resolved namespace — and every subcommand (`--version`, `kat`, `selftest`, `measure`, `bundle`, `attest`, `gate`, `justify`, `gc`, `m0-run`, registered by their own beads) reads them from there; no subcommand defines its own spelling of these paths (a built bundle is written to `--bundle`, its pin to `--pin`, `attest init` creates `--attest` — cairn-m0-e0s.10).
- `src/cairn/log.py`: the one logger every CLI and gate decision uses — structured records on stderr `{ts, step, ids/hashes, verdict, reasons, wall_ms}`; level from `--log LEVEL` or `CAIRN_LOG` (default INFO); DEBUG adds subprocess argv and stdin/stdout/stderr BLAKE3 digests; never logs substrate paths into a skill's environment. Tests assert on records via pytest caplog.
- Shared fixture: `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` = `{bits:60, seed:1, p, a, b, n, P:[x,y]}` as decimal strings, generated ONCE in gp with EXACTLY the call sequence cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins for bits > 50 (the PARI PRNG state is advanced by `ellsea(E,1)` and by 60-bit `ellcard`, so any other call order yields a different curve — probed 2026-08-21): `setrand(1); p = randomprime([2^59, 2^60]); tries = 0; while(1, a = random(p); b = random(p); if((4*a^3 + 27*b^2) % p == 0, next); tries++; E = ellinit([a,b], p); n = ellsea(E, 1); if(n && isprime(n), break)); if(ellcard(E) != n, error("confirm")); P = random(E)` run as `/opt/homebrew/bin/gp -q -f -s 64M gen60.gp`; the grounding brief's mode-1 row predicts `tries = 45` at seed 1 and the file records it; committed with `origin: author_supplied`, the gp script (`tests/vectors/gen60.gp`) and the tries count in the file; the stack-fact smoke test (c) below, the verifier's 60-bit and forced-crash tests (cairn-m0-e0s.8) and the gate plan's crash fixture (cairn-m0-e0s.11) read it; cairn-m0-e0s.6 asserts `toy_curve(60,1)` reproduces it bit-for-bit.
- Smoke tests (integration, `tests/integration/test_smoke.py`):
  (a) cypari2: `ellinit([-3,1],5)` → `ellcard` = 7 (PARI user manual usersch3.tex:29031-29032, upstream_vendored);
  (b) gp subprocess: `subprocess.run([GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s","64M"], input="print(ellcard(ellinit([-3,1],5)))")` → stdout `7`, rc 0;
  (c) stack fact: `ellcard` on the committed 60-bit curve (`tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json`) succeeds under allocatemem (cypari2) and under `gp -s 64M` and equals the vector's `n`; control: the same under `gp -s 8M` fails with a stack-overflow message on stderr and rc 0 (the gp exit-0-on-fatal fact).
- Unit tests (`tests/unit/test_pari_module.py`): `run_gp` builds argv `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",<stack>]` and passes `shell=False`; `run_gp(..., timeout_s=0.001)` on a good input raises `GpTimeout` and leaves no zombie (`os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)` raises `ChildProcessError` afterwards); the global CLI options parse with their defaults for every registered subcommand and parse to the same values whether placed before or after the subcommand token; a missing `GP_BIN` (monkeypatched path) raises the typed error before any spawn; `log.py` emits a parseable record at INFO and adds digests only at DEBUG.
- `uv run cairn --version` prints the version; `uv run cairn --version --log DEBUG` emits at least one structured record on stderr.

DESIGN: the PARI handle lives in one module so allocatemem runs once; all gp invocations go through `cairn.pari.run_gp(args, stdin, *, timeout_s)` returning (rc, stdout, stderr) — on timeout it kills the child, reaps it and raises `GpTimeout` (the verifier maps that to `FAIL timeout`, cairn-m0-e0s.8) — so later beads share one spawn path; all logging goes through `cairn.log.get(step)` so every bead's records have one shape.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Dev dependencies: `uv add --dev pytest hypothesis` (Hypothesis 6.165.x installs cleanly under Python 3.14 on this Mac — probed 2026-08-21; atheris does not: its build needs a custom libFuzzer clang, so Hypothesis is the only fuzz/property engine at M0 and no atheris target exists anywhere in M0).
- `tests/conftest.py` (created here, shared by every bead): Hypothesis profiles `settings.register_profile('ci', max_examples=500, deadline=None, print_blob=True)` and `settings.register_profile('dev', max_examples=50, deadline=None)`, loaded from `HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE` (default `ci`); `.hypothesis/` gitignored; the autouse `isolation_guard` fixture (snapshot of `deploy/` and `var/` before/after each test — any delta fails; a call-through spy on `subprocess.Popen` failing the test when `argv[0]` is neither `sys.executable` nor `cairn.pari.GP_BIN`; `CAIRN_DB*` scrubbed from the environment); the autouse `json_test_log` fixture routing `cairn.log` records to `tmp_path/test.log.jsonl` with phase/step/wall_ms and the `db_snapshot(substrate, label)` helper; the golden harness `assert_golden(name, text)` reading `tests/goldens/<name>.golden`, rewriting it when `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` is set, otherwise failing with a unified diff and writing `<name>.actual` (gitignored); and `load_vector(name)` for `tests/vectors/*.json`.
- Golden: `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` is a golden of volatility 3 — deterministic under pinned PARI 2.17.4 / libpari 2.17.2 and the pinned call sequence, platform-dependent only through libpari's PRNG, so a libpari bump may legitimately move it; `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` (created here) records its generator command (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gp -q -f -s 64M tests/vectors/gen60.gp`), gp/libpari versions, date and that note; regeneration is `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_smoke.py -k curve60` followed by an attributed commit naming the libpari version; without the env var the smoke test (c) fails when gp's live output differs from the file.
- Harness self-test `tests/unit/test_golden_harness.py`: `assert_golden` on a temp golden differing from its actual fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS` (the failure message carries a unified diff) and rewrites the file with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`; `isolation_guard` fails a test body that creates a file under `deploy/` and one that spawns `/bin/echo` (both exercised through `pytester` so the guard's own failure is observed, not inferred).

title: M0: gate bundle (separate read-only SQLite, content-addressed) + deployment pin (0444+append-only) + attestation file (0644+append-only) + attestation digest/offset check + tier gate predicate (TierRefused; bundle≠pin fails closed; uncertified/yanked refused; ticket bundle-hash mismatch re-mints) + OS write-boundary tests + waiver-cannot-advance fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §4, §5): a gate that silently fails open manufactures the appearance of enforcement. The gate bundle is content-addressed, opened read-only by the orchestrator process, its hash pinned at deployment in an operator-owned file the process user cannot write, and recorded in every gate-run record; a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed whoever rewrote it. The tier gate reads only launch-supplied inputs (cost profile at inputs, budget, hypothesis key/method identity) plus substrate-resolved ones (self-test standing, ticket) and judges against gate-owned objects; a refusal is a `TierRefused` record, not an exception to retry around. Operator decisions 8 (one OS user at M0 → mode/flags only; what that refuses is recorded by bead m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2) and 9 (ticket carries bundle hash; mismatch ⇒ re-mint) bind.

WHAT (`src/cairn/bundle.py`: build, pin, `GateBundle`; `src/cairn/attest.py`: `attest init/append`, `attestation_record_matches`, `visible_review_verdicts`; `src/cairn/tiergate.py`: `TierGate`)
- `bundle/*.json` source: `verifier {backend_path:"/opt/homebrew/bin/gp", stack_ceiling:"64M", timeout_s:30, accept:{rc:0, stdout:"OK", stderr_empty:true}}` (a structured object the driver evaluates field by field, cairn-m0-e0s.8 — never a string it would have to evaluate) plus the `verifier_script` object (the bytes of `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`, kind `verifier_script`, so the verifier's script is pinned and hash-recorded in every gate run; the driver materializes it from the bundle, cairn-m0-e0s.8); `tiers {boundary_table:[{tier:0,max_core_s:1},{tier:1,max_core_s:3600},{tier:2,max_core_s:3600000},{tier:3,max_core_s:null}] (one unit, core-seconds, throughout; M0 defaults, CONJECTURE; 3 600 000 core-s is the ≈10³ core-hour Tier-2/3 edge of PLAN §5; a launch's tier is the first row whose max its production cost does not exceed), ceiling_multiplier:4, tier1_cumulative_edge:null}` (edge set at M1, decision 10); `gate_plan` (ordered steps with expected results — bead m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; its crash fixture embeds the committed 60-bit curve `(p,a,b)` from `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` as decimal strings for the `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` entry at `8M` and its `64M` control); `waivable_checks: []` (no admission gate is waivable; the waiver fixture consults this set); `auditor {f:0.01,bits:20}`; `lean {permitted_axioms:["propext","Classical.choice","Quot.sound"]}` (stored, unused until M1); `role_templates:{}`, `allow_lists:{}` (M1).
- `uv run cairn bundle build --src bundle/` (writes the global `--bundle` path, default `deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`; no `--out`): one row per object (kind, canonical bytes, hash); bundle hash = H('cairn/gate-bundle/v1' ‖ sorted (kind,hash) pairs); deterministic (build twice → same hash). `uv run cairn bundle pin` (reads the global `--bundle`, writes the global `--pin`, default `deploy/gate-bundle.pin`) writes the hash, chmods pin and bundle 0444 and sets `uappnd` on the pin (macOS; probed 2026-08-21: with the flag standing the owner's `chmod` is refused too; re-pinning is the operator's act and needs `chflags nouappnd` first). `uv run cairn attest init` (creates the global `--attest` path, default `deploy/attestations.log`; no positional path) creates the file mode 0644 and sets `uappnd` (appendable by the owner, not overwritable, not truncatable, not re-modable while flagged; 0444 would refuse the append — cairn-m0-e0s.2 probe 3), and appends as record 0 the gate plan's fixture waiver `{kind:'waiver', target_kind:'hypothesis_key', target: H(W), check:'tier_gate', reason:'gate-plan fixture', issued_by:'attest init', expires_at:'9999-12-31T23:59:59Z'}` — `W` is the fixture hypothesis object the bundle's `gate_plan.fixtures` carries (cairn-m0-e0s.11) — so the `waiver_cannot_advance` step reads an operator-written record at a known offset instead of appending one per run, a shape that survives the second OS user of M3; elsewhere than macOS it logs loudly and skips the flag.
- `GateBundle.open(path, pin_path)`: opens `file:...?mode=ro`; recomputes the hash from rows; compares to the pin; mismatch → `BundlePinMismatch`, and every gate run refuses with a `gate_runs` row `gate='bundle_open', result='refused', reasons=['bundle-hash-ne-pin']`.
- `attestation_record_matches(file, offset, digest) -> bool`: reads the length-prefixed canonical record at `offset`, compares BLAKE3; `visible_review_verdicts(statement_hash)` filters rows through it (used by bead m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; the same function serves `yank_records`/`salts` at M1). Operator append path: `uv run cairn attest append --kind review_verdict ...` appends the canonical record and mirrors the substrate row with digest+offset (at M0 the same OS user runs both; the boundary is the file mode/flag + the digest rule); `--kind waiver` appends the file record and mirrors no row at M0 (no M0 reader consumes waivers — `waivable_checks` is empty; the waiver table arrives with the human queue, cairn-m1-cqt.7), the form cairn-m0-e0s.12's waiver-moves-no-tag test uses.
- `TierGate.admit(launch) -> Admitted | TierRefused`; launch = `{cost_profile, inputs, budget_remaining, hypothesis_key, method_identity, statement_hash?, skill_identity_hash, declared_tier}`; the production cost at inputs is `cost_profile.evaluate(inputs).expected_core_s` (a `cairn.profile.CostProfile`, the module cairn-m0-e0s.6 creates — this bead depends on it for the type alone; a profile whose `evaluate` raises `ProfileUndeclared` at the launch's inputs is a refusal, `profile-undeclared`; the tier-gate tests use synthetic `CostProfile` instances, never the toy-curve one); resolves `certified(skill_identity)` and `not yanked(skill_identity)` (predicates in cairn-m0-e0s.4); selects the ticket (Tier 0: none; Tier 1: a hypothesis object, plus the claim statement node where a claim exists, recorded in the substrate — the §8 presence check and the §7 statement pre-filters that also condition the Tier-1 ticket arrive at M1; Tier 2/3 kinds are M1 — absent ⇒ refuse); refuses when `declared_tier > ticket_tier + 1` (`tier_refusals` row), when declared tier < the tier the boundary table assigns the production cost at the launch's inputs, when uncertified or yanked, when `evaluate(inputs).expected_core_s + expected_verification_core_s` (cairn-m0-e0s.6's `Evaluation`) > remaining budget; the predicates do not short-circuit — `reasons` lists every one that holds, in the fixed order `profile-undeclared` (which leaves the cost-dependent predicates unevaluated), `ticket-absent`, `tier-two-above`, `boundary-table`, `uncertified`, `yanked`, `budget`, `ticket-bundle-mismatch` — and the launch is admitted iff `reasons` is empty, so a gate-plan self-test step asserts the reason it plants whatever else its fixture launch lacks (cairn-m0-e0s.11); every decision is a `gate_runs` row (gate='tier_gate', result admitted|refused) with bundle hash + pin hash; a ticket whose recorded bundle hash ≠ current bundle hash → refused `ticket-bundle-mismatch`, and that refusing decision is also the re-mint of decision 9 at M0: because the Tier-1 ticket here is a substrate node no gate run produced (the hypothesis object), the gate re-selects it under the current bundle and writes the fresh `tickets` row in the same decision, so the next launch on that key reads the fresh row and is admitted — a stale row blocks a key for exactly one refusal, never permanently (from M1 a ticket a gate run produced, a ladder table, is re-minted only by re-running that gate under the current bundle, tier-below work the refusal leaves to the next launch). The gate is the only writer of `tickets` rows (table in cairn-m0-e0s.5): on admission it mints the row for the ticket it selected — at M0 `{hypothesis_key, method_identity, statement_hash?, tier: 0, kind: 'hypothesis_object', node_hash: the hypothesis object's hash, bundle_hash: the current bundle hash}` — when no row under the current bundle exists, and a later launch reads the most recent row for that hypothesis key and method identity; the stale-bundle test pre-writes a row under another bundle hash for a key whose hypothesis object is recorded, asserts the refusal (`ticket-bundle-mismatch` in `reasons`) and that a fresh row under the current bundle now exists beside the stale one (rows are append-only, cairn-m0-e0s.5), then asserts that the same launch re-issued is admitted reading the fresh row. UNIT (`tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py`, pure): the predicate's truth table over (declared tier, ticket tier, boundary-table tier at cost, certified, yanked, budget ok, ticket bundle matches) — each refusal reason reached by exactly the rows that should reach it; the boundary-table lookup at its edges (1, 3600, 3 600 000 core-s: a cost exactly at an edge stays in the lower tier, one unit above it moves up).

title: M0: declarative gate plan runner with planted-failure self-tests run before the gates (verifier xP≠Q + forced crash; canonicalizer KATs; waiver-cannot-advance); ordered scopes where an earlier failure blocks later steps; fail closed on invalid/missing config
description:
WHY (PLAN §4 gate discipline; §13 M0): every gate ships a planted-failure self-test (a fixture that must FAIL and one that must PASS) run before the gate itself; gates run from a declarative plan with expected results and ordered scopes — an earlier failure blocks later steps and records why; invalid or missing gate config fails closed; a green result whose provenance is weaker than required cannot strengthen a claim. The first gate self-tests at M0 are the verifier's planted `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures and the canonicalizer's known-answer vectors for both keys.

WHAT (`src/cairn/gateplan.py`)
- Plan = ordered steps from the gate bundle, e.g. `[{step:'canon_kat', cmd:'kat canon', expect:'pass'}, {step:'verifier_selftest_pass', fixture:'corpus-1 x=3', expect:'OK'}, {step:'verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q', fixture:'corpus-1 x=4', expect:'FAIL xP-ne-Q'} (`corpus-1` = the F_5 instance `(p=5, a=2, b=1, n=7, P=(0,1), Q=(3,3))` embedded in the bundle as decimal strings — `a` already reduced from the corpus file's `-3`, cairn-m0-e0s.7/.8 — never read from `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json` at gate time), {step:'verifier_selftest_crash', entry:'crash_selftest', fixture:'curve60_seed1 (p,a,b) as decimal strings embedded in the bundle; the committed vector of cairn-m0-e0s.1', stack:'8M', expect:'FAIL backend-crash'} (the real backend really overflowing: rc 0, empty stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr — `verify()` itself prints OK at 8M because it never calls `ellcard`, probed 2026-08-21, which is why the crash step calls the script's `crash_selftest` entry, cairn-m0-e0s.8), {step:'verifier_selftest_crash_control', entry:'crash_selftest', same curve, stack:'64M', expect:'OK'} (the must-PASS half: the crash entry is a live computation, not a stub), {step:'waiver_cannot_advance', expect:'no-ticket'}, {step:'tier_gate_selftest_two_above', expect:'TierRefused(tier-two-above)'}]`. The two tier-gate steps run against the real `TierGate` (cairn-m0-e0s.10) from `gate_plan.fixtures`, carried in the bundle so they are pinned and hash-recorded: two synthetic hypothesis objects `A` and `W` (canonical per cairn-m0-e0s.3, `target_family:'gate_plan_fixture'`, `method_identity:{interface_version:'gate_plan_fixture/1', params:{}}`), a fixture `CostProfile` with one declared size at 0.01 core-s, and a fixture `skill_identity_hash`; the launch shape is `{declared_tier, hypothesis_key, method_identity: the object's, cost_profile: the fixture profile, inputs: its one size, budget_remaining: 1e6, skill_identity_hash: the fixture identity}`. `waiver_cannot_advance`: asserts `attestation_record_matches(attest, 0, BLAKE3 of the fixture waiver)` — the record `cairn attest init` appended naming `H(W)` (cairn-m0-e0s.10); a missing or altered record 0 fails the step — then admits the launch with `declared_tier:1, hypothesis_key:H(W)` (no hypothesis object recorded for `W`) and observes `TierRefused` with `ticket-absent` among its reasons and no `tickets` row for `H(W)` (= `no-ticket`), and asserts the bundle's `waivable_checks == []`. `tier_gate_selftest_two_above`: records `A` in `hypothesis_objects` if absent (the harness writer; a same-hash insert is a no-op, cairn-m0-e0s.4) so `H(A)` holds a Tier-0 ticket, then admits the launch with `declared_tier:2, hypothesis_key:H(A)` and observes `TierRefused` whose reasons include `tier-two-above` and a `tier_refusals` row — the gate collects every applicable reason (cairn-m0-e0s.10), so the uncertified fixture identity does not mask the planted one; each step writes a `gate_runs` row (gate='gate_plan', plan_step, result pass|fail|blocked, reasons, bundle+pin hash); the first failing step blocks all later steps (`result='blocked', reasons=['blocked-by:<step>']`).
- `GatePlan.run(bundle, substrate) -> PlanResult`; non-zero exit on any failure; a missing plan, an unknown step kind, or a plan lacking any of the required self-test steps (`verifier_selftest_pass`, `verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q`, `verifier_selftest_crash`, `verifier_selftest_crash_control`, `canon_kat` — the must-PASS and must-FAIL halves of the verifier's pair, the crash pair, and the canonicalizer's vectors; §4's discipline is a pair per gate, so a plan holding only the FAIL half is refused) → fail closed before any step runs (`missing-required-selftest`).
- `uv run cairn gate selftest [--json]`; bead m0-e2e-slice (cairn-m0-e0s.14) calls it first. Logging: one record per step (step, expected, observed, gate_runs row id, wall_ms) at INFO; fixture stdin/stdout/stderr digests at DEBUG; `--json` emits the same per-step fields.
TESTS (integration, `tests/integration/test_gateplan.py`): full plan green against the built bundle; temp bundle without the `xP≠Q` step → plan refuses to run; a weakened accept predicate (`{rc:0, stdout:null, stderr_empty:false}` in a writable bundle copy re-pinned for the test, so the gate under test is the real driver + the real gp with a weakened predicate, not a mock) → plan fails at `verifier_selftest_crash` (the rc-0 overflow is now read as OK) and later steps are `blocked` — the `xP≠Q` step still fails correctly under that predicate because gp quits 1 there, which is exactly why the rc-0 crash step exists; a bundle copy whose `verifier_script` has the `ellmul(E,P,x)==Q` check removed (re-pinned) → plan fails at `verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q` and later steps are `blocked`; malformed plan row → fail closed; expected-result mismatch recorded with stdout/stderr digests; caplog holds one record per step.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_gateplan_validation.py`, no gp): plan validation — a missing required step, an unknown step kind, a duplicate step name and an expected-result value outside the vocabulary are each refused before any step runs with the named reason; the blocking logic over a synthetic step sequence — the first failure blocks every later step and each blocked row names the blocker (`blocked-by:<step>`); a plan with zero steps is refused.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Fuzzing (`tests/unit/test_gateplan_fuzz.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500, no gp, no substrate writes): the loader `GatePlan.load(plan_rows)` over arbitrary plan documents — `st.lists(st.dictionaries(st.text(), st.recursive(st.none() | st.booleans() | st.integers() | st.text(), lambda c: st.lists(c) | st.dictionaries(st.text(), c))))`, `None`, a scalar, an empty list, a 10 000-step plan — and over mutations of the committed plan (drop one required step, duplicate a step name, rename `expect`, unknown `step` kind, `expect` outside the vocabulary, reorder so the FAIL half precedes the PASS half, a fixture field of the wrong type) — every malformed plan is refused with `PlanInvalid(reason)` naming the first offending path before any step runs, with zero `gate_runs` rows written (a reader connection counts them) and zero subprocess spawns (the `isolation_guard` spy); only the exact committed plan loads; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/gateplan_mutants.py`: `loader_skips_unknown_steps` (ignores instead of refusing) and `loader_runs_valid_prefix` (runs steps up to the first bad one) — each killed; seed corpus `tests/fuzz_corpus/gateplan/` holds the planted negatives (missing `verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q`, FAIL-half-only plan, duplicate step, vocabulary miss, empty plan, `expect: null`) replayed as `@example`s.
- Property over the blocking logic (`tests/unit/test_gateplan_validation.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500): for any outcome sequence from `st.lists(st.sampled_from(['pass', 'fail']), min_size=1, max_size=20)` applied to synthetic steps, with `i` the first `fail` index, rows `< i` are `pass`, row `i` is `fail`, every row `> i` is `blocked` with `reasons == ['blocked-by:<step_i>']`, and with no `fail` every row is `pass` — kills `continue_after_failure` and `blocks_name_wrong_step`.
- Failure-path convergence: the plan-validation refusals (missing required step × 5, unknown kind, duplicate name, vocabulary miss, zero steps) are one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(plan_delta, expected_reason)` with `match=`; the two weakened-bundle integration cases (weakened accept predicate, weakened `verify.gp`) stay separate since each re-pins a different bundle and observes a different failing step.
- Every integration plan run calls `db_snapshot` (`gate_runs` per result) after the run, so a step that wrote two rows or none is visible in `test.log.jsonl`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run cairn gate selftest --json` exits 0 listing every step `pass` with its gate_runs row id (the crash step's observed `FAIL backend-crash` and its control's `OK` both count as `pass` against their expectations); `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gateplan.py tests/unit/test_gateplan_validation.py -q` green.
- Planted negative: a weakened-accept-predicate bundle copy must make the plan FAIL at the crash step and block the rest; a bundle copy whose `verify.gp` lacks the `xP == Q` check must make it FAIL at the `xP≠Q` step; a plan missing a required self-test step must be refused before any step runs; an attestation file lacking the fixture waiver at record 0 must fail the waiver step; the two-above step must observe `tier-two-above` in the refusal's reasons (a `TierRefused` for another reason alone fails the step); the crash fixture returning anything but `FAIL backend-crash`, or its control returning anything but `OK`, fails the plan. Asserted.
- No-Claim: a green plan proves the fixtures behave as planted on this machine at this bundle hash; it is not evidence about any claim.
- `tests/unit/test_gateplan_fuzz.py` green at ≥ 500 examples: every malformed plan is refused with `PlanInvalid` naming its path, zero `gate_runs` rows and zero spawns; `loader_skips_unknown_steps` and `loader_runs_valid_prefix` killed; `tests/fuzz_corpus/gateplan/` replayed; the blocking property holds over random outcome sequences with `continue_after_failure` and `blocks_name_wrong_step` killed; the validation refusals are one parametrized test.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.

title: M0: justify(evidence, statement_hash): kind→max-class map, producer-standing ceiling, coverage check (interval containment / categorical equality / assumption ⊆), lattice violations, review_verdict digest rule, refuted-version rule, append-only attributed tag history
description:
WHY (PLAN §7): the tag is derived, never set. Each evidence kind has a maximum class; `justify` checks the evidence's declared target names the exact statement hash, its declared population is a superset of the statement's scope and its assumptions a subset of the statement's, and returns a typed justification or a lattice/coverage violation — never a boolean. A weaker class may inform, never justify. Every tag transition is an append-only attributed tag_history row with an evidence pointer. PROVEN needs a `lean_artifact` AND an `approve` `review_verdict` on the same statement hash whose digest matches the attestation file (else the row is absent).

WHAT (`src/cairn/justify.py`; tables from bead m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5)
- `justify(evidence, statement, ctx) -> Justification | CoverageViolation | LatticeViolation | Absent | Pending`. Classes are totally ordered SPECULATION < CONJECTURE < STRONG-EMPIRICAL < PROVEN.
- Kind → max class: `lean_artifact` + visible `approve` verdict on the same statement hash → PROVEN (without it → `Pending(human_review)`, claim stays at its pre-review tag); `ladder_table` verdict KEEP — or KEEP_IN_SAMPLE when the statement's `scope.size_interval ⊆ evidence.in_sample_sizes` — whose own attempt carries a passed reproducibility record (`repro_records.passed = 1` reached through `evidence.repro_record_hash`) → STRONG-EMPIRICAL; same table with the record absent or grade `AuditOnly` → CONJECTURE ceiling; any other table verdict → justifies nothing; `statistical` / `repro_node` → ≤ STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the declared population, EXCEPT for a statement whose typed fields carry a cost model (`claim_statements.quantities.cost_model IS NOT NULL`) → CONJECTURE ceiling; `model_proof` → ≤ CONJECTURE; `counterexample_hunt_record` SURVIVED → CONJECTURE (a ticket, not a promotion), KILLED → the statement moves to terminal `refuted` with the evidence pointer.
- Producer-standing ceiling: producer is a certified skill revision (its `skill_certificates.selftest_summary`, cairn-m0-e0s.4/.7) with no STRONG-EMPIRICAL basis covering the attempt's inputs — every `corpus_origins` entry `author_supplied`, `randomized_arm` false, and no `cross_check` whose `independent_range` (an axis-aligned interval record over the input fields, `{bits:[lo,hi]}`, read with the same containment comparator the coverage check uses) contains the attempt's inputs → cap at CONJECTURE; a gate-bundle producer or a gate run is not capped by this rule.
- Coverage: `population.target_family == scope.target_family`; numeric intervals of the population contain the statement's (size and every parameter range); `population.assumptions ⊆ statement.assumptions`; otherwise CoverageViolation (typed: which field).
- Disowned evidence (attempt `disowned_at` not null) → Absent; an `AuditOnly` node (by `effective_grade`, cairn-m0-e0s.4) → the CONJECTURE ceiling, never Absent and never higher (inadmissible above it, §3 — the done-when's AuditOnly case). Refuted statement + any positive class → LatticeViolation. A class offered above the kind's maximum (e.g. `statistical` for PROVEN) → LatticeViolation.
- `derive_tag(statement_hash)` = strongest class justified by any evidence node targeting it; writes a tag_history row (actor 'gate:justify', evidence pointer, typed justification); a downgrade requires an evidence pointer; nothing edited in place.
- `review_verdicts` visible only through `attestation_record_matches` (`src/cairn/attest.py`, bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10). A waiver is not evidence: `evidence_nodes.kind` admits no waiver kind, `justify` reads the attestation file for `review_verdict` records and nothing else, and `derive_tag` is unchanged by a waiver record naming the statement hash — the claim half of §4's waiver-cannot-advance fixture (the tier half is cairn-m0-e0s.10's).
- CLI: `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash>` prints the derived tag and the justifying evidence hash. Logging: every `justify` call logs (statement hash, evidence hash, kind, result type, class or violation field) and every `derive_tag` logs the transition through `cairn.log`.
TESTS (integration, real substrate + attestation file; `tests/integration/test_justify.py`) — the §13 done-when set, named test ids: synthetic statement S (family 'toy_curve', size [30,50], assumptions {A1}); ladder_table KEEP on [30,60] ⊇ scope with passed repro record → STRONG-EMPIRICAL; repro absent → CONJECTURE; repro record with `passed = 0` → CONJECTURE; grade AuditOnly → CONJECTURE; population [40,50] → CoverageViolation(size_interval); assumptions {A1,A2} → CoverageViolation(assumptions); family mismatch → CoverageViolation(target_family); statistical offered for PROVEN → LatticeViolation; statistical for a cost-model statement → CONJECTURE ceiling; KEEP_IN_SAMPLE with scope ⊆ in_sample_sizes → STRONG-EMPIRICAL and with scope ⊄ → nothing; lean_artifact + approve verdict with matching digest → PROVEN; same with a forged digest → verdict absent → not PROVEN (Pending); disowned ladder_table → Absent; a producer with an all-`author_supplied` synthetic selftest_summary → CONJECTURE ceiling while the same node from a producer with a covering arm is not capped; statement moved to refuted then a KEEP table offered → LatticeViolation; a waiver record appended through `cairn attest append --kind waiver` naming S → `derive_tag(S)` unchanged and `tag_history` gains no row; tag_history holds one row per transition and refuses UPDATE; caplog holds one record per call.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_justify_rules.py`, pure): the coverage comparator (interval containment incl. equal endpoints, categorical equality, assumption subset incl. empty set); the kind→max-class table; the class order; the producer-standing rule over synthetic summaries, including a summary whose only covering basis is a cross-check whose `independent_range` contains the attempt's inputs (not capped) and the same summary with the inputs outside that range (capped).

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Metamorphic relations (`tests/unit/test_justify_properties.py` over the pure rules, Hypothesis ≥ 500 per relation; generators from `tests/factories.py`: scopes with `size_interval = [lo, hi]`, `lo ≤ hi` from `st.integers(20, 80)`, `param_ranges` as 0–3 axis-aligned intervals, `assumption_set` from `st.frozensets(st.sampled_from(['A1'..'A6']))`, `target_family` from a three-word vocabulary, evidence kinds from the CHECK vocabulary, `repro ∈ {absent, passed, failed}`, grade ∈ {Replayable, Verifiable, AuditOnly}, producer summaries over origins/arm/cross_check; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/justify_mutants.py`, each relation's `test_mutant_<name>_is_killed` asserting the relation fails on it): MR-W widening — if `justify(e, S)` is a `Justification`, then for any `e'` equal to `e` with every population interval widened (`[lo - d1, hi + d2]`, `d ≥ 0`, equal endpoints included) `justify(e', S)` is never a `CoverageViolation` and has the same class — kills `comparator_strict_containment` (requires strict `⊂`, failing on equal endpoints) and `comparator_checks_lo_only`; MR-A assumption — for any `e` with `justify(e, S)` a `Justification`, adding any assumption `a ∉ S.assumption_set` to `e.population.assumptions` always yields `CoverageViolation(assumptions)` — kills `comparator_assumptions_superset` (tests `⊇` instead of `⊆`); MR-M monotone in evidence strength — for any statement and any list of evidence nodes, `class(derive_tag)` is non-decreasing as nodes are appended (the terminal `refuted` path excluded from the generator) and never exceeds `max_class(kind)` of the strongest node — kills `derive_takes_last_node` (uses the most recent node) and `kind_table_off_by_one` (`statistical → PROVEN`); MR-C ceiling — for any evidence node and any producer summary, `class ≤ kind_ceiling`, and a summary that is all-`author_supplied` with `randomized_arm = False` and no `cross_check` whose `independent_range` contains the attempt's inputs caps at CONJECTURE — kills `producer_rule_ignores_range` (treats any cross_check as covering); composite MR-W ∘ MR-A (widen, then add an assumption ⇒ still `CoverageViolation(assumptions)`).
- Fuzz-shaped robustness (same file, ≥ 500): the coverage comparator over arbitrary interval records (`lo > hi`, missing axes, extra axes, negative sizes, huge ints, `None` endpoints) returns a typed violation naming the field or a `Justification`, never an unhandled exception.
- Failure-path convergence: the kind → max-class table is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(kind, verdict, repro, grade, expected_class_or_violation)`; the §13 done-when cases stay one parametrized integration test in `tests/integration/test_justify.py` whose `ids=` are the bead's named case ids, since their setups differ only in data from `tests/factories.py`; every justify integration case calls `db_snapshot` (`tag_history` row count) after `derive_tag`.
- Layer: relations and tables unit (pure comparator, kind table, producer rule); `derive_tag`, the attestation-file visibility rule and the waiver-moves-no-tag case integration (real substrate, real attestation file).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_justify.py tests/unit/test_justify_rules.py -q` green with every done-when case named in the test ids; `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash>` prints the derived tag and justifying evidence hash.
- Planted negative: statistical→PROVEN must be a LatticeViolation; missing or failed repro must cap at CONJECTURE; forged verdict digest must not yield PROVEN; a coverage gap must be a CoverageViolation; an all-`author_supplied` producer must be capped; a waiver record must move no tag. Any of these returning a positive class fails the bead.
- No-Claim: all evidence is synthetic; no ladder, Lean artifact or real verdict exists at M0; the Tier-2/3 branches (KEEP_IN_SAMPLE scope, hunt records) are exercised by construction only.
- MR-W, MR-A, MR-M, MR-C and MR-W∘MR-A in `tests/unit/test_justify_properties.py` green at ≥ 500 examples; every mutant in `tests/mutants/justify_mutants.py` (`comparator_strict_containment`, `comparator_checks_lo_only`, `comparator_assumptions_superset`, `derive_takes_last_node`, `kind_table_off_by_one`, `producer_rule_ignores_range`) killed — a survivor fails the bead; the comparator never raises unhandled on 500 arbitrary interval records.
- The kind → max-class table and the §13 done-when cases are each one parametrized test (the done-when case ids are the `ids=`), all built from `tests/factories.py`; `tag_history` counts land in `test.log.jsonl` via `db_snapshot`.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.

title: M0: GC roots table + reachability over lineage; only blobs collectable; cache completeness on missing blob; dry-run CLI
description:
WHY (PLAN §3 retention): keep lineage + certificates forever, GC the giant intermediate blobs once their derivation is recorded and the result verified. Roots = recipes, ledger rows, certificates, recorded divergences; liveness = reachability from roots over lineage edges; only blobs are collectable; a cached result is served only if every blob it references is present, otherwise recomputed.

WHAT (`src/cairn/gc.py`; the `roots(root_kind, node_hash)` table is defined in bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4, which also inserts the recipe, certificate and divergence roots as it writes them): `add_root(root_kind, node_hash)` for the ledger-row kind that M1 writes; `reachable()` = BFS from every roots row over `lineage` treated as undirected — the conservative reading of 'reachability from roots over lineage edges': a blob is live while any path of `lineage` rows joins it to a root, so a rooted recipe's input blobs (`'input'` edges) and its attempts' output blobs (`'output_of'`/`'member'` edges, the set cairn-m0-e0s.9 writes) are both kept, and a blob with no path to any root is the only collectable thing; `collect(dry_run)` deletes blob rows not reachable and writes a `gc_runs` record (count, bytes, at); nodes/edges/attempts/receipts/roots are never deleted (append-only triggers from cairn-m0-e0s.4 refuse). `uv run cairn gc [--dry-run]`; each run logs (roots counted, reachable count, candidate count, bytes, dry_run) through `cairn.log` and at DEBUG the candidate hashes.
TESTS (integration, `tests/integration/test_gc.py`): recipe R (root) → attempt → manifest → blob B1; orphan blob B2; `collect` removes B2, keeps B1; delete B1's row manually (simulated loss) → `serve(R)` returns None (recompute path; links to the substrate serve test); collect on an empty DB is a no-op; a certificate node is a root and its blob survives; a non-reproducible recipe's two attempts are both rooted as divergences (cairn-m0-e0s.4) and survive; `--dry-run` deletes nothing and lists exactly the orphan.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_gc_reachability.py`, pure): `reachable()` over synthetic root sets and edge lists — a chain, a diamond, a cycle (terminates; every member reachable once), a disconnected component (unreachable), a root with no edges (reachable alone), and an empty root set (nothing reachable); the collectable set equals blobs minus reachable in each case.

TEST PLAN (shapes)

title: M0: execute and record the stack facts M0 stands on (SQLite WAL + busy timeout, macOS append-only flag, pin/attestation write boundary, gp exit/arity facts)
description:
WHY (PLAN §16, §13 M0 first sentence): a stack fact no probe has executed is CONJECTURE until research/grounding/ records the run, and each of these sits under a gate — the single-writer contract relies on WAL + busy timeout (§3); the human path relies on the orchestrator's process user being unable to write the pin or the attestation file (§4); the M2 chain checkpoint relies on the append-only flag binding against truncation (§3). Inherited stack claims are wrong at a meaningful rate when executed.

WHAT: probes as pytest integration tests (they re-run forever) plus the human-readable brief `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` with one row per fact: fact, tag (PROVEN-by-probe / STRONG-EMPIRICAL / CONJECTURE / OPEN), exact command, observed output, date, OS (`sw_vers`, `uname -a`), filesystem (APFS). The same brief later gains the tries table (cairn-m0-e0s.6) and the rho-at-60-bits section (cairn-m0-e0s.15); each bead writes its own section.

PROBES
1. SQLite WAL (`tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py`): file DB under tmp_path; `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` returns `wal`; the writer holds `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` plus one uncommitted INSERT and a second connection's SELECT returns (WAL readers never wait on a writer). Control: the same under `journal_mode=DELETE` → the reader's SELECT raises `OperationalError: database is locked` after its timeout. The writer MUST open with `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` — probed 2026-08-21 under the Homebrew python3 (CPython 3.14.3, SQLite 3.52.0) and re-probed with the same six-cell result under the project's uv-managed interpreter (CPython 3.14.0, SQLite 3.50.4 — the one `uv run pytest` uses; the brief's row names the interpreter and SQLite version the test ran under): under DELETE a plain `BEGIN` or `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` holding an uncommitted INSERT leaves the reader unblocked (the writer holds RESERVED and readers still take SHARED), so the control arm would agree with the treatment and the probe would fail by its own rule; only EXCLUSIVE blocks readers, and under WAL all three BEGIN kinds leave the reader free.
2. Busy timeout: A holds a write txn; B with `PRAGMA busy_timeout=500` attempts a write → waits ≈0.5 s then `OperationalError: database is locked`; with A committing after 0.2 s, B succeeds. Record measured waits.
3. Append-only flag (`tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py`, macOS `chflags uappnd` on APFS), on a file owned by the current user. Pre-probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6 (the test must reproduce this table): mode 0644 + `uappnd`: `open(path,'a')`+write succeeds, `os.open(O_WRONLY|O_APPEND)` succeeds, `open(path,'w')` → EPERM, `open(path,'r+')` → EPERM, `os.truncate` → EPERM, `os.chmod` by the owner → EPERM while the flag stands; mode 0444 + `uappnd`: append → EACCES (the mode denies write before the flag is consulted), overwrite/truncate/chmod → EPERM; mode 0444 without the flag: every write → EACCES but the owner's `chmod` succeeds; mode 0644 without the flag: everything succeeds (control). Consequence: the attestation file is 0644 + `uappnd` (appendable, not overwritable, not re-modable while flagged), the pin is 0444 + `uappnd` (nothing writes it, nothing re-modes it while flagged). Record honestly: with ONE OS user (operator decision 8) the same user can `chflags nouappnd` and then chmod/truncate, so at M0 the flag refuses truncation and re-moding by the process but does not bind against a process that clears it — that half is OPEN until M3 introduces the second OS user; the Linux equivalent (`chattr +a`) is OPEN until the M1 container exists.
4. Write boundary: pin file 0444 + `uappnd` → `open(pin,'w')`, `open(pin,'a')`, `os.truncate(pin)`, `os.chmod(pin, 0o644)` all raise PermissionError for the (non-root) owner; attestation file 0644 + `uappnd` → `open(...,'w')`/`'r+'`/truncate/chmod raise, `open(...,'a')` by the same user succeeds (record: at M0 "cannot write" = cannot overwrite/truncate/re-mode; an append by the harness process is not refused until the two-user shape — the digest/offset rule in bead m0-justify (cairn-m0-e0s.12) is what makes a harness-appended forgery useless, and bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate (cairn-m0-e0s.10) tests that). Also: `os.unlink(pin)` and `os.rename(pin, …)` → EPERM while `uappnd` stands (probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6 = Darwin 25.6.0, APFS: `rm` and `mv` both refused with `Operation not permitted`), the same for the attestation file, and both succeed after `chflags nouappnd` — so the pin cannot be replaced by rename while flagged, and every test that flags a file under tmp_path clears the flag in teardown or pytest's basetemp cleanup fails. Control: after `chflags nouappnd` the owner's chmod, unlink and rename succeed — the recorded gap.
5. gp facts (`tests/integration/test_grounding_gp.py`): gp exits 0 on `1/0` with the message on stderr; a 3-arg user function called with 2 args runs with the third zero-filled; a successful run under `gp -q -f -s 64M <file.gp>` fed one stdin line writes 0 bytes to stderr (probed 2026-08-21: stdout `OK`, rc 0 — the empty-stderr accept predicate of cairn-m0-e0s.8 is satisfiable); `quit(1)` yields rc 1 with the FAIL line on stdout and empty stderr; a 60-bit `ellcard` under `-s 8M` yields rc 0, empty stdout and `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr; gp's own startup needs more than 2 MB of stack — `gp -q -f -s 2M verify.gp` (and `-s 1M`) exits 1 with `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout and `*** the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr before reading stdin; `verify(...)` on the 60-bit instance `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` prints OK with rc 0 under `-s 3M`, `-s 8M` and `-s 64M` (probed 2026-08-21: `verify.gp` never calls `ellcard`, so an 8 MB ceiling does NOT crash the verifier — the forced-crash fixture is the `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` entry of cairn-m0-e0s.8, which is a 60-bit `ellcard`); `verify(2,0,1,3,0,1,0,1,1)` (p = 2) dies with a fatal `ellisoncurve: incorrect type in checkell (t_VEC)` at rc 0 because `ellinit([0,1],2)` returns `[]` — the fact behind the driver's `p > 3` pre-spawn rule; reference grounding brief pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §3.
6. PARI PRNG consumption (same test file; the fact cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins its call sequence on): after `setrand(s)` and a fixed prefix of draws, `random(2^64)` is unchanged by an intervening 40-bit `ellcard(E)` but changed by an intervening 40-bit `ellsea(E)`, and changed by an intervening 60-bit `ellcard(E)` or `ellsea(E,1)` (probed 2026-08-21 on gp 2.17.4); the test asserts each of the four comparisons in gp and in cypari2 (libpari 2.17.2).

7. CPython reap order (`tests/integration/test_grounding_subprocess.py`; the fact cairn-m0-e0s.9 stands on): a child that exits 3 is spawned with `Popen`; after `communicate()` returns, `os.wait4(pid, 0)` raises `ChildProcessError` (`communicate()` reaps through `wait()` — subprocess.py 1212/1239/2152, CPython 3.14.0 under uv, read 2026-08-21) and `proc.returncode == 3`; control: the same child with stdout/stderr redirected to files and no `communicate()` — `os.wait4(pid, 0)` returns the status word (`os.waitstatus_to_exitcode` → 3) with rusage, and a `proc.wait()` issued afterwards returns 0 (the `_try_wait` → `ChildProcessError` → 0 path that would record every crash as exit 0).

DESIGN: the tests are the executable record; the brief is written by hand from their output with tags. Probes 3–4 skip with an explicit reason when not on macOS (the M1 Linux container gets its own probe bead). No generator script for the brief. Every probe logs its command and observed output through `cairn.log` at INFO so the brief's rows can be copied from the test log.

- Every probe logs through `json_test_log` so `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` rows are copied from `test.log.jsonl` (command, observed output, wall_ms), never retyped.
- Layer: all integration (real filesystem flags, real SQLite files, real gp, real CPython subprocess); no unit tests here, nothing to mock.

title: M0: canonical typed encoding + BLAKE3 content addressing: recipe key, hypothesis key, identity bundle, environment manifest; known-answer vectors for both keys
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): REFUTED-by-hash and every cache hit are exactly as sound as the canonicalizer — two logically equal recipes that hash differently are a bug that silently under-reports dead ends. The canonicalizer's known-answer vectors are one of the first gate self-tests (§13 M0) and run before any gate.

WHAT (`src/cairn/canon.py`, `src/cairn/keys.py`)
- Canonical encoding: typed, domain-separated; fields in fixed declared order; maps and sets sorted by canonical key bytes; every variable-length field length-prefixed (u64 LE length ‖ bytes); ints as sign byte ‖ big-endian magnitude, length-prefixed (arbitrary precision — curve coordinates are 60–254-bit); strings UTF-8 NFC; blob references as `(hash, size)`; NO unknown fields (a key the schema does not declare raises `CanonError` at write time); no floats in keys (numeric profiles are declared as rationals or strings).
- Hash: BLAKE3-256 over `domain_tag ‖ canonical_bytes`. Fixed domain tags: `cairn/recipe-key/v1`, `cairn/hypothesis-key/v1`, `cairn/node/v1`, `cairn/identity-bundle/v1`, `cairn/env-manifest/v1`, `cairn/selftest-cert/v1`, `cairn/gate-bundle/v1`, `cairn/instance/v1` (the verifier instance `(p,a,b,n,P,Q)` — cairn-m0-e0s.8 and .14 hash it with this tag), `cairn/chain/v1` (reserved for M2).
- Recipe key = H over `(skill_identity_hash, inputs: sorted map name → (hash,size), seed, tool_versions: sorted map, container_digest, salt)`. `skill_identity_hash` = hash of the §2 identity bundle `{interface_version, implementation_revision, tool_digests, container_digest, numeric_profile}` so a changed executable is a different recipe. On the M0 machine (no container) `container_digest` = hash of the environment manifest `{os: sw_vers+uname, python, cypari2, libpari (pari.version()), blake3, gp_binary_sha256}` — never empty (empty raises).
- Hypothesis key = H over the typed hypothesis object `{target_family, claimed_property_or_cost_model (or claim statement hash), method_identity (interface version + canonical params — NEVER implementation revision), declared_parameter_ranges, sampling_distribution?}`; per-run seeds, ladder instances and free-text fields are excluded by schema.
- Schemas: one `Schema` (ordered tuple of (name, type)) per object kind; encode walks the schema, never the dict, so undeclared keys surface as a set difference.
- Known-answer vectors `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` (≥6): recipe key (two logically-equal spellings with different dict/set order → same expected hash), hypothesis key, identity bundle, env manifest (fixed synthetic values), node hash, and a negative vector (one byte changed in the canonical input → a DIFFERENT expected hash, asserted not-equal). Generated once, committed; origin recorded `author_supplied` (they pin the encoding against drift; they are not an external oracle).
- `uv run cairn kat canon` runs the KAT and exits 0/1, logging one record per vector (name, expected, computed, match) — the entry bead m0-gate-plan-selftests (cairn-m0-e0s.11) calls.
- Tests (`tests/unit/test_canon.py`): permuting insertion order never changes the hash; undeclared field raises; empty container digest raises; ints round-trip through a decoder used only by tests; every vector matches; the same object under two different domain tags hashes differently.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Golden KATs: `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` is an exact golden of volatility 1 (pure bytes + BLAKE3; deterministic and platform-independent; the env-manifest vector uses fixed synthetic field values, never the live `pari_versions()`); generated once by `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/unit/test_canon.py -k kat`, reviewed by hand once (a hex dump of each vector's canonical bytes beside its hash in `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` with the generator command and blake3 version), committed; compared exactly through `assert_golden` on every run; a regenerated KAT lands only in an attributed commit whose message names the encoding change (this KAT is the canonicalizer gate self-test of cairn-m0-e0s.11, so a silent change would move every recipe key); guard test `tests/unit/test_canon.py::test_kat_guard_rejects_drift` copies the vector file to tmp_path, flips one hex byte, points the loader at the copy and asserts the KAT comparison fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS` — the permanent form of the manual flip-one-byte step, which stays in the close comment as well.
- Metamorphic + property-based (`tests/unit/test_canon_properties.py`, Hypothesis, ≥ 500 examples per relation under the `ci` profile; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/canon_mutants.py`, each relation's `test_mutant_<name>_is_killed` asserting the relation fails on its mutant; a relation whose mutant survives is deleted, not kept decorative): MR-1 permutation invariance — for any schema-valid object `o` (generator: `st.fixed_dictionaries` per schema with map/set fields drawn then shuffled by `st.permutations`), `encode(shuffle_maps_and_sets(o)) == encode(o)` — kills `dict_order_encoder` (walks insertion order); MR-2 idempotence — `encode(decode(encode(o))) == encode(o)` and two fresh encoder instances agree — kills `salted_encoder` (mixes a counter into the output); MR-3 length-prefix injectivity — for any byte string `s` and two different split points `i ≠ j`, `encode([s[:i], s[i:]]) ≠ encode([s[:j], s[j:]])` (no concatenation ambiguity), with `encode(['ab','c']) ≠ encode(['a','bc'])` as an `@example` — kills `concat_encoder` (drops the u64 LE length prefix); MR-4 domain separation — for any object and any two distinct tags from the fixed tag list, `H(tag1 ‖ c) ≠ H(tag2 ‖ c)` — kills `untagged_hasher`; MR-5 field sensitivity — changing any one declared field to a different valid value changes the hash — kills `first_n_fields_encoder` (encodes a schema prefix); MR-6 integer encoding — for `i ∈ st.integers(-(2**300), 2**300)`, `decode_int(encode_int(i)) == i`, `len(encode_int(i)) == len(encode_int(-i))` for `i ≠ 0`, and `encode_int(0)` is one fixed byte string — kills `fixed_width_int_encoder` (truncates above 64 bits; the 254-bit coordinates are why).
- Fuzzing (same file, Hypothesis structure-aware, ≥ 500 examples): `encode(schema, payload)` for `payload` from `st.recursive(st.none() | st.booleans() | st.integers() | st.binary() | st.text(), lambda c: st.lists(c) | st.dictionaries(st.text(), c), max_leaves=50)` — never raises anything but `CanonError`; any payload holding a key outside the schema raises `CanonError` naming that key (`match=`); any float anywhere in a key object raises `CanonError`; every schema-valid payload round-trips through the test-only decoder (`decode(encode(p)) == p`); `st.text()` plus explicit NFC/NFD pairs: `encode('\u00e9') == encode('e\u0301')`. Seed corpus `tests/fuzz_corpus/canon/` holds the planted negatives (undeclared field, empty `container_digest`, float in key, NFD string, 300-bit int, `[]` vs `[b'']`, `['ab','c']` vs `['a','bc']`) replayed as `@example`s before random generation.
- Layer: all unit (pure library, pyramid); `uv run cairn kat canon` is the one integration touch and asserts exit code and one log record per vector only — it never re-asserts vector values.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_canon.py -q` green; `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` committed; `uv run cairn kat canon` prints PASS, exit 0, one log record per vector.
- Planted negative: the negative KAT vector must NOT match; an undeclared field must raise `CanonError`; an empty `container_digest` must raise; two domain tags over one object must not collide. Once at close: flip one byte in a stored vector locally, confirm the KAT test fails, revert; record in the close comment.
- No-Claim: KATs are self-generated; green proves stability of this encoding, not agreement with any external standard; collision resistance is BLAKE3's claim.
- Hypothesis relations MR-1..MR-6 in `tests/unit/test_canon_properties.py` green at ≥ 500 examples each; every named mutant in `tests/mutants/canon_mutants.py` (`dict_order_encoder`, `salted_encoder`, `concat_encoder`, `untagged_hasher`, `first_n_fields_encoder`, `fixed_width_int_encoder`) is killed by its relation — a surviving mutant fails the bead; the fuzz target raises nothing but `CanonError` over 500 structure-aware payloads, names the undeclared key, refuses floats and round-trips every valid payload; `tests/fuzz_corpus/canon/` replayed.
- Golden: `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` compares exactly through `assert_golden`; `test_kat_guard_rejects_drift` proves a one-byte change fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`; `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` carries the generator command, blake3 version and a hex dump per vector; a regenerated KAT appears only in an attributed commit naming the encoding change.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.
