title: M0: substrate store (SQLite + BLAKE3): nodes/blobs/lineage, recipes, attempts, execution receipts, cache bits, statuses, salt, disowned, replay grade, certificate slot; single writer + WAL; M1 column fixtures
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): a result not in the substrate does not exist to the claims DB. Provenance is a storage property: every launch appends an attempt; nothing is overwritten; a cached value is served only from a verified attempt; a failure is a record, not a memo. This schema is the shape every later milestone plugs into.

WHAT (`src/cairn/substrate.py`, SQL in `src/cairn/schema.sql`; hashes via bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3)
Tables
- `blobs(hash PK, size, bytes, created_at)` — the only collectable kind (bead m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13).
- `nodes(hash PK, kind, canonical BLOB, replay_grade CHECK IN ('Replayable','Verifiable','AuditOnly'), producer_identity, created_at)`; `lineage(child_hash, parent_hash, edge_kind)` append-only. Every content-addressed object of any typed table (claims layer included, cairn-m0-e0s.5) also has a `nodes` row with the same hash and kind, so lineage and GC see one graph.
- `roots(root_kind CHECK IN ('recipe','ledger_row','certificate','divergence'), node_hash, PRIMARY KEY(root_kind,node_hash))` — the GC roots table (§3: recipes, ledger rows, certificates and recorded divergences are roots); defined here because `mark_non_reproducible` below roots both attempts; reachability and collection are cairn-m0-e0s.13.
- `recipes(recipe_key PK, skill_identity_hash, inputs_manifest_hash, seed, tool_versions_hash, container_digest, salt, do_not_cache INT)`; inserting a recipe also inserts its `roots('recipe', recipe_key)` row.
- `attempts(attempt_id PK, recipe_key, output_manifest_hash NULL, receipt_hash NULL, status CHECK IN ('RUNNING','OK','FAIL','DISAGREE','BUDGET_EXCEEDED','SKILL_YANKED','INTERRUPTED'), replay_grade, verifier_result_hash NULL, certificate_hash NULL, skip_cache_lookup INT, disowned_at NULL, inadmissible INT DEFAULT 0, started_at, ended_at NULL)`. `RUNNING` is the in-flight status an attempt is inserted with (`ended_at IS NULL`); exactly one UPDATE is permitted per row — `RUNNING` → a terminal status, setting `ended_at`, `output_manifest_hash`, `receipt_hash` together (the runner, cairn-m0-e0s.9, performs it; its `startup_scan()` performs `RUNNING` → `INTERRUPTED` for every row with `ended_at IS NULL` before any new launch, PLAN §4); a second UPDATE raises.
- `receipts(receipt_hash PK, gate_bundle_hash, start_mono, end_mono, cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s, wall_s, peak_rss_bytes, scratch_bytes_written, exit_status, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, tool_digests_hash)` — written by the harness writer only (bead m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9).
- `skill_certificates(identity_bundle_hash PK REFERENCES nodes(hash), cert_hash UNIQUE, transcript_hash, env_manifest_hash, selftest_summary, at)` — the §2 certificate slot; `selftest_summary` is canonical JSON `{corpus_origins: [per-case per-field origins], randomized_arm: bool, cross_check: {axis, independent_range (an axis-aligned interval record over the input fields, e.g. {bits:[0,50]})} | null, pass, floor}` that `justify`'s producer-standing ceiling reads (cairn-m0-e0s.12); rows are written by the skill self-test (cairn-m0-e0s.7), which first persists the identity bundle itself as `nodes(hash = identity_bundle_hash, kind = 'identity_bundle', canonical = the §2 bundle bytes)` so every `skill_identity_hash` a recipe, attempt or ticket names resolves to a stored object (a certificate row naming an identity with no `nodes` row is refused); the certificate's own content-addressed object is `nodes(hash = cert_hash, kind = 'skill_certificate')` with a lineage edge `cert_hash → identity_bundle_hash` (`edge_kind = 'certifies'`), and inserting one also inserts `roots('certificate', cert_hash)`. `cert_hash = H('cairn/selftest-cert/v1' ‖ identity_bundle_hash ‖ transcript_hash ‖ env_manifest_hash)`, each field length-prefixed per cairn-m0-e0s.3 — the identity hash is inside the certificate, so a certificate copied from one revision's row onto another's cannot verify. Predicates here: `certified(identity_bundle_hash)` ⇔ a row exists AND `cert_hash` recomputed from the row's own fields equals the stored one (a tampered or transplanted row is uncertified); `yanked(identity_bundle_hash)` ⇔ a `yank_records` row names it. The tier gate (cairn-m0-e0s.10) reads both.
- `yank_records(yank_id, skill_identity_hash, reach_predicate, ruling_ref NULL, record_digest, file_offset, created_at)`, `salts(class_key PK, salt, record_digest, file_offset)` — schema only at M0; both are human-path records (operator decision 5: yanks and salt issuance are human-only, like waivers), hence the attestation digest+offset columns that cairn-m0-e0s.10's `attestation_record_matches` reads at M1.
- `escrow(attempt_id PK, declared_production_cost, declared_verification_cost, reserved, spent_at NULL, released_at NULL, ceiling_multiplier)` — M0 writes and reads every column in a fixture; enforcement is M1 (§13).
Behavior
- Cache serve path `serve(recipe_key)`: the most recent attempt with status OK, not disowned, not inadmissible, recipe not `do_not_cache`, every referenced blob present (else None → recompute). `status ≠ OK ⇒ never cached` is part of the serve query, not a convention (RUNNING, FAIL, DISAGREE, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, SKILL_YANKED, INTERRUPTED are all excluded by that one predicate). `skip_cache_lookup` callers always record a fresh attempt.
- Replayable recipe with two OK, non-disowned attempts whose output manifests differ → `mark_non_reproducible(recipe_key)`: both attempts kept, both rooted (`roots('divergence', attempt output node)`), both `inadmissible=1`.
- Immutability: `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers → `RAISE(ABORT,'append-only')` on nodes, recipes, receipts, lineage, roots, skill_certificates, yank_records, salts; on attempts the only permitted UPDATEs are (i) the single RUNNING→terminal close, (ii) the one-time NULL→value set of `disowned_at`, (iii) the one-time 0→1 set of `inadmissible`; any other UPDATE and every DELETE raises.
- Single writer: `Substrate.open(path, role='writer'|'reader')`; writer sets `journal_mode=WAL`, `busy_timeout=5000`, `synchronous=NORMAL`; reader opens `file:...?mode=ro` URI; one writer object per process (module guard). Workers never receive the writer.
- `weaken_grade(node_hash, to)`: a grade moves only down the order Replayable > Verifiable > AuditOnly and the move is a new append-only `grade_history(seq PK AUTOINCREMENT, node_hash, from_grade, to_grade, reason, at)` row — `nodes.replay_grade` is never updated in place (the append-only trigger forbids it); `effective_grade(node_hash)` = the latest `grade_history` row's `to_grade`, else the node's column, and every grade reader (`justify`'s AuditOnly rule, the tier gate's ticket rule) reads `effective_grade`; a strengthening, or a move to the same grade, raises.
- Every write and every serve decision logs through `cairn.log` (table, hash, status / served-or-why-not).

title: M0: exemplar skill toy_curve(bits, seed) → (p,a,b,n,P) on PARI via cypari2: algorithm-axis cross-check (≤50 bits), postcondition arm, declared cost profile measured over ≥50 seeds, content-addressed I/O
description:
WHY (PLAN §2, §13): the exemplar is the one skill built end to end at M0 — typed interface, fixed version, content-addressed I/O, captured seed, self-test, declared cost profile; every research skill from M1 copies its shape. Operator decision 1: PARI-only at M0 with the BSGS-vs-SEA *algorithm* cross-check valid for bits ≤ 50; no second implementation until M1 (gmpy2).

INTERFACE (`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py`): `run(bits: int, seed: int) -> ToyCurveOutput{p, a, b, n, P=(x,y), tries, cross_check: {axis:'algorithm', independent_range:{bits:[0,50]}, result:'agree'|'untested'} (`independent_range` is an axis-aligned interval record over the input fields — the shape `justify`'s containment comparator reads, cairn-m0-e0s.12 — never a string), status:'OK'|'DISAGREE'}`. Declared cost profile is a typed object `CostProfile{tier: 0, production: {model: 'c_ln_p_tries', per_size: {bits: {mean_tries, sd_tries, per_try_s, mean_wall_s}} for bits ∈ {30,40,50,60} from the ≥50-seed table below — `mean_wall_s` is the mean wall of a full `python -m cairn.skills.toy_curve` subprocess launch at that size (interpreter start + cypari2 import + `allocatemem` included)}, verification: {grade: 'Replayable', cost_model: 'same_as_production'}}` with `evaluate(bits) -> {expected_wall_s, expected_core_s, expected_verification_core_s}` (the first two = `mean_wall_s` at the launch's size; the third = `expected_core_s`, a Replayable Tier-0 node's verification under the §3 re-run policy being one more production run — the number the tier gate adds to production against the remaining budget and the runner writes to `escrow.declared_verification_cost`, cairn-m0-e0s.10/.9) — the number the tier gate compares against the boundary table (cairn-m0-e0s.10) and the runner multiplies by 4 for its ceiling (cairn-m0-e0s.9), so interpreter start never trips the ceiling; a launch whose `bits` is not a declared size raises `ProfileUndeclared` before any spawn; `CostProfile`, its `Evaluation{expected_wall_s, expected_core_s, expected_verification_core_s}` result and `ProfileUndeclared` are defined in `src/cairn/profile.py`, created by this bead — the tier gate (cairn-m0-e0s.10) and the runner (cairn-m0-e0s.9) import `cairn.profile`, never `cairn.skills.toy_curve`, and `toy_curve.py` holds only the toy-curve instance with its measured `per_size` table; replay grade Replayable; `do_not_cache=False`. Module entry `python -m cairn.skills.toy_curve` reads canonical JSON inputs on stdin and writes canonical JSON output on stdout (the runner contract, bead m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9); the skill never opens the substrate and receives no substrate path.

IDENTITY (the §2 bundle cairn-m0-e0s.3 hashes under `cairn/identity-bundle/v1`; `toy_curve.identity_bundle()` returns it and `skill_identity_hash` is its hash — the value cairn-m0-e0s.7 certifies, cairn-m0-e0s.9 launches under and cairn-m0-e0s.10/.14 test with `certified()`): `interface_version = 'toy_curve/1'` (the method name a hypothesis object's `method_identity` carries); `implementation_revision` = BLAKE3-256 over the length-prefixed `(path ‖ bytes)` pairs, sorted by path, of `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py`, `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json` and `src/cairn/pari.py` — content-derived, never a declared string, so an edited executable, corpus or arithmetic seam is a new identity, uncertified until its own self-test passes (the property cairn-m0-e0s.7's negative (c) and the tier gate's uncertified-revision refusal rest on); `tool_digests = {gp_binary_sha256, cypari2, libpari}` from `cairn.pari.pari_versions()` and the `GP_BIN` file; `container_digest` = the environment-manifest hash of cairn-m0-e0s.3; `numeric_profile = null` (an integer-only skill). Unit test (`tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py`): the identity hash is stable across two computations and changes when one byte of any of the three files changes.

ALGORITHM — CALL SEQUENCE PINNED (matches the grounding brief's bench.gp / bench_cypari2.py, which gave bit-identical p,a,b,n,tries in gp and cypari2; the PARI PRNG state is part of the contract — probed 2026-08-21 on gp 2.17.4: at 40 bits `ellcard(E)` leaves the PRNG state unchanged while `ellsea(E)` advances it, and at 60 bits both `ellcard(E)` and `ellsea(E,1)` advance it, so any call added inside the loop, or reordered after it, changes every later draw): `setrand(seed)`; `p = randomprime([2^(bits-1), 2^bits])`; `tries = 0`; loop: `a = random(p); b = random(p)`; if `4a³+27b² ≡ 0 (mod p)` continue (a singular pair is not counted); `tries += 1`; `E = ellinit([a,b], p)`; bits ≤ 50 → `n = ellcard(E)` (generic path, milliseconds), accept iff `isprime(n)`; bits > 50 → `m = ellsea(E,1)` (early abort: returns 0 on a small factor), accept iff `m ≠ 0 and isprime(m)`, with `n = m`. After the loop, in this order: bits > 50 only — confirm `ellcard(E) == n` once under the 64 MB stack (a mismatch is `status='DISAGREE'` exactly like the cross-check below, though at 60 bits both calls are SEA and no independence is claimed); then `P = random(E)` (non-identity); then the postcondition arm; then, bits ≤ 50 only, the algorithm-axis cross-check — after P is drawn and never inside the loop. Expected tries for seeds 1,2,3 (the bench rows; the integration test asserts them): 30 bits 48/148/20; 40 bits 40/52/57; 50 bits 36/11/220; 60 bits 45/72/140. All order calls go through the `cairn.pari.ellcard` / `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrappers (cairn-m0-e0s.1) — the one seam where a test plants a disagreement.
Algorithm-axis cross-check (bits ≤ 50 only, once, on the accepted curve): `ellsea(E)` (SEA) must equal `ellcard(E)` (generic BSGS-family); on mismatch return `status='DISAGREE'` (never OK, never cached) carrying both transcripts and digests for a substrate node; NO silent retry with a third tool. For bits > 50 `result='untested'` (at 60 bits `ellcard` is itself SEA — agreement by construction, no independence claimed). A cross-check that has never disagreed is reported in the self-test ledger as untested-for-disagreement, never as passing.
Randomized postcondition arm on every output: `isprime(n)`; `ellmul(E,P,n)==[0]`; `n ∈ [p+1-2√p, p+1+2√p]`; `ellisoncurve(E,P)`.
Content-addressed I/O: inputs `{bits, seed}` canonicalized; output manifest = canonical bytes of the output hashed (bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3).
Cost-profile constant: `uv run cairn measure toy-curve-tries --sizes 30,40,50,60 --seeds 50` records, for ≥50 seeds per size, the in-process tries and wall AND the wall of a fresh subprocess launch per seed (the `mean_wall_s` the profile declares) (60 bits included: the skill's declared range reaches the 60-bit rung and its per-try cost there is the `ellsea(E,1)` early-abort path at ≈ 0.3 ms per rejected curve, so the in-process 60-bit loop over 50 seeds finishes in well under a minute, and the per-seed subprocess launches across the four sizes add ≈ 200 × ≈ 0.3 s ≈ one more minute; the constant is declared per size) (mean, sd, min, max, wall) into its own section of `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md`; the declared profile cites that table (STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the sample), never the 3-seed table (20–220 tries; CONJECTURE on means). Expected shape: geometric, sd ≈ mean, expected tries ≈ c·ln p.
Stack: `cairn.pari` applies `allocatemem(64_000_000)` once before any 60-bit work.
Logging: every run logs (bits, seed, tries, n bit-length, cross_check result, status, wall) through `cairn.log`; a DISAGREE logs both transcript digests.

title: M0: toy_curve self-test: vendored known-answer corpus (4 cases, origin per field) + ledger + pass floor, randomized_postcondition arm, golden certificate, byte-equal double run, certificate recorded → revision certified
description:
WHY (PLAN §2): a skill's self-test is (i) a vendored known-answer corpus with a per-case ledger `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap` and a committed pass floor only an attributed update may raise; (ii) a golden certificate = hash over the canonical transcript of the corpus and the exact outputs — a changed implementation behind the same interface needs a fresh certificate and a mismatch fails closed; (iii) every nondeterminism source pinned and a byte-equal double run asserted. A corpus supplied only by the author is not a self-test (`author_supplied` alone caps results at CONJECTURE, enforced by `justify`'s producer-standing rule). A revision is launchable only once its self-test passed and its certificate is recorded; the tier gate refuses an uncertified revision exactly as a yanked one.

CORPUS (`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json`, origin per field; sources pinned in research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §4). Origin rule: a field copied from an upstream document is `upstream_vendored`; a field completed locally (a point chosen here, a scalar or Q computed here) is `author_supplied` and is re-checked by a postcondition at every self-test run — it is never trusted; the `randomized_postcondition` origin names only the seeded arm below (inputs drawn from a seed committed after the implementation revision is content-addressed). Field forms: the corpus file stores each field as the upstream document writes it (case 1 `a = -3`, case 4 `Px = -33`); cypari2 accepts those in-process, and whenever a corpus case is handed to the Tier-0 verifier driver (the gate plan's `corpus-1` steps, cairn-m0-e0s.11) it travels as an `Instance`, which reduces `a, b` and every coordinate into `[0, p)` (case 1 reaches gp as `a = 2`; cairn-m0-e0s.8).
1. F_5: `y² = x³ − 3x + 1`, `n = 7` — `upstream_vendored` (PARI 2.17.4 usersch3.tex:29031-29032). `P=(0,1)`, `Q=3P=(3,3)`, `x=3` derived locally — origin `author_supplied`; every self-test run asserts `ellorder(E,P)=7` and `ellmul(E,P,3)=Q`; never trusted as vendored (PLAN §13: a locally completed triple is author_supplied).
2. GF(101): `y² = x³ + 90x + 44`, `n = 89` (prime), `x = 2`, `Q = 2P` — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4529-4537 + constructor.py:790-791). `P` is not explicit upstream (`E.gens()[0]`) → chosen locally as the least-x non-identity point; origin `author_supplied` for P with the per-run postcondition `ellorder(E,P)=89`, `2P=Q`.
3. 150-bit: `p = 1427247692705959881058285969449495136382746771`, `E=[1,1]`, `P=(831623307675610677632782670796608848711856078, 42295786042873366706573292533588638217232964)`, `n = 1427247692705959881058262545272474300628281448` (composite, even) — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4680-4686); membership/cardinality/big-int path; no x.
4. Negative control: `E=[1,0]/GF(419)`, `P=(-33,8)`, order 21, card 420 — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:822-827); asserts `n·Q ≠ O` for a point outside the order-21 subgroup — the must-FAIL fixture of the postcondition.
RANDOMIZED_POSTCONDITION ARM per run: generate a 30-bit curve from a seed committed AFTER the implementation revision is content-addressed (seed = first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision ‖ 'selftest-seed')), assert the postcondition arm (`isprime(n)`, `n·P = O`, Hasse interval, on-curve). Verifier-shaped arm on the same curve, run through the real Tier-0 verifier driver (bead m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8, real gp subprocess) under the verifier config of the gate bundle — backend path, stack ceiling, timeout, accept predicate and the `verifier_script` bytes all read from `GateBundle.open(--bundle, --pin)` (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; the self-test spells no verifier invocation of its own, since that invocation is a gate-bundle field, PLAN §4), so a `BundlePinMismatch` aborts the self-test before any case runs (exit ≠ 0, no certificate row); the `--json` output and the log records name the bundle hash the arm ran under (the transcript stays the §2 corpus-and-outputs record), which is why the operator sequence builds and pins the bundle before `cairn selftest` (cairn-m0-e0s.14): 20 draws `x`, `Q = xP` → driver returns OK; 20 draws `x' ≠ x` → FAIL `xP-ne-Q`; both counts are fields of the transcript. This bead owns wiring that arm (dependencies on cairn-m0-e0s.8 and cairn-m0-e0s.10); the verifier's own planted self-test belongs to the gate plan (cairn-m0-e0s.11).
LEDGER + FLOOR: each case → `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap`; `pass_floor` (M0: 4/4 + both arms) lives in the corpus file; only an attributed change (commit with reason) may raise it.
CERTIFICATE: `transcript` = canonical bytes of (corpus, exact outputs, ledger, arm outcomes); `cert = H('cairn/selftest-cert/v1' ‖ identity_bundle_hash ‖ transcript_hash ‖ env_manifest_hash)` (each field length-prefixed; the identity hash is inside the certificate, so it cannot be transplanted onto another revision's row); the self-test first persists the identity bundle as `nodes(hash = identity_bundle_hash, kind = 'identity_bundle')`, then writes the `skill_certificates` row `(identity_bundle_hash, cert_hash, transcript_hash, env_manifest_hash, selftest_summary, at)` together with its `nodes(hash = cert_hash, kind = 'skill_certificate')` row, the lineage edge certificate → identity bundle and `roots('certificate', cert_hash)` (table, rows and the `certified()` predicate are bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4); `selftest_summary` = `{corpus_origins (per case, per field), randomized_arm: true, cross_check: {axis:'algorithm', independent_range:{bits:[0,50]}}, pass: 4, floor: 4}` — what `justify`'s producer-standing ceiling reads (cairn-m0-e0s.12). DOUBLE RUN: the whole self-test runs twice; canonical transcripts byte-equal (no timestamps inside the transcript; seed, hashers, clock pinned). Runtime target < 5 s, Tier-0.
CLI: `uv run cairn selftest toy-curve [--json]` (the global `--db`, default `var/substrate.sqlite`, names the substrate the certificate row is written to, and the global `--bundle`/`--pin`, defaults `deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`/`deploy/gate-bundle.pin`, name the bundle whose verifier config the verifier arm runs under — cairn-m0-e0s.1) exits 0 and prints the certificate hash; the integration test (`tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py`) builds and pins its own bundle under tmp_path through the build/pin functions of cairn-m0-e0s.10 and clears `uappnd` in teardown; a corpus schema check requires `origin` on every field; every case and arm logs (case id, ledger entry, observed vs expected) through `cairn.log`.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_selftest_cert.py`, no PARI): the corpus schema check refuses a case missing an `origin` on any field and a ledger value outside `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap`; the certificate composition over fixed synthetic identity/transcript/env hashes equals a committed vector in `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` and changes when the identity hash is swapped (the transplant property); the seeded-arm seed (`first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision ‖ 'selftest-seed')`) is stable for a fixed revision and differs for a bumped one.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Goldens: `tests/goldens/toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden` = the canonical transcript bytes (hex, one line per corpus case and arm) and `tests/goldens/toy_curve_floor.golden` = `{pass: 4, floor: 4, arms: {postcondition: 'pass', verifier: {ok: 20, fail: 20}}}` are exact goldens of volatility 2 — deterministic because seed, hashers and clock are pinned and no timestamp enters the transcript; `tests/goldens/toy_curve_certificate.golden` holds the certificate hash with the env-manifest hash it was minted under and is volatility 4 (it folds in `env_manifest_hash`, which depends on libpari, the gp binary digest and the OS), so the test compares the transcript exactly and recomputes `cert` from (golden transcript hash, live identity hash, live env hash), asserting the live certificate equals that recomputation and equals the golden value only when the live env manifest hash equals the recorded one (otherwise it logs `env-manifest-differs` and the golden is valid for the recorded platform only); every regeneration goes through `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py` and an attributed commit naming the reason — this IS PLAN §2's rule that only an attributed update may raise the floor or re-mint the certificate; `tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py::test_transcript_golden_guard` fails when the live transcript differs from the golden without the env var; PROVENANCE.md rows for all three.
- Failure-path convergence: the four-case ledger is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(case_id, expected_ledger, postcondition)` with `ids=['F5','GF101','bits150','negative_control']`; the planted negatives (a)–(f) stay separate because each perturbs a different input.
- Fuzzing (`tests/unit/test_selftest_corpus_fuzz.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500, no PARI): the corpus schema check over arbitrary JSON documents (`st.recursive`) and over mutations of the real corpus (drop `origin` from one field, set `origin` to an unknown word, ledger value outside `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap`, `pass_floor` above the case count or negative or a string, a fifth case with a duplicate id, an empty cases list) — refuses with the typed `CorpusSchemaError` naming the offending path (`match=`) before any PARI call (a call-through spy on `cairn.pari.ellcard`/`ellsea`/`ellorder` asserts zero calls on every refusal) and never raises an unhandled exception; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/selftest_mutants.py`: `schema_checks_first_case_only` and `floor_not_validated` (accepts `pass_floor > len(cases)`), each killed; seed corpus `tests/fuzz_corpus/selftest_corpus/` holds those negatives as files replayed by `@example`.
- Conformance: this bead's self-test, ledger, floor, certificate and double run are clauses S2-04..S2-08 of the §2 harness (cairn-m0-e0s.16); the harness runs them against the real self-test through the real runner, real gp and real substrate, and this bead's tests are not repeated there.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py tests/unit/test_selftest_cert.py -q` green; `uv run cairn selftest toy-curve --json` prints `{pass:4, floor:4, arms:{postcondition:'pass', verifier:{ok:20, fail:20}}, certificate:<hash>, bundle:<hash>, double_run:'byte-equal'}`; a `skill_certificates` row exists for the identity bundle hash and `certified(identity_bundle_hash)` is true; `nodes` rows exist for both the identity bundle and the certificate and `roots` holds `('certificate', cert_hash)`; its `selftest_summary` carries the per-field origins (case 1 P/Q/x and case 2 P as `author_supplied`); the `--json` `bundle` field and the verifier-arm log records name the bundle hash the arm ran under, equal to the pinned bundle's.
- Planted negative: (a) alter one expected output in a temp copy of the corpus → certificate mismatch, exit ≠ 0, `certified()` false; (b) the negative-control point must FAIL `n·Q = O` (if it passes, the test fails); (c) bump `implementation_revision` without re-running → `certified()` false for the new identity hash; (d) the verifier arm's 20 `x' ≠ x` draws must all FAIL (one OK fails the self-test); (e) a corpus case missing an `origin` must be refused by the schema check before any case runs; (f) a pin that does not match the bundle must abort the self-test before any case runs — exit ≠ 0 and no `skill_certificates` row (a certificate written under a mismatched pin fails the test).

title: M0: Tier-0 verifier subprocess (gp): membership n·Q=O then xP==Q; affirmative acceptance (rc==0 AND stdout==OK AND stderr empty); arity/field validation before spawn; explicit stack ceiling; forced crash → FAIL; gate-read instance, submitter supplies x only
description:
WHY: "No submission without a passing verifier (xP == Q) subprocess" is an invariant (CLAUDE.md). Acceptance is affirmative, never residual: gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow — PROVEN by probe) and zero-fills missing arguments, so rc==0 is not evidence of anything. The instance is gate-read: the curve, n, P, Q come from the claim statement node or dispatch record, never from the submitter, who supplies x alone — `xP == Q` on an instance the worker chose is a true statement about the wrong problem (PLAN §4).

WHAT (`src/cairn/verifier.py`, `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`)
- `verify.gp` (shape from grounding brief §3) ships two entry points. `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)`: `ispseudoprime(p)` → nonsingular → `ellisoncurve(E,P)` and `(E,Q)` → `ellmul(E,Q,n)==[0]` (membership FIRST — PARI's generic `elllog` can loop when no solution exists; the verifier never calls a log) → `ellmul(E,P,x)==Q`; prints exactly one line `OK` or `FAIL <reason-codes>`; `quit(0|1)`. `crash_selftest(p,a,b)`: `ellcard(ellinit([a,b],p)); print("OK"); quit(0)` — the gate's forced-backend-crash fixture, reachable only from the gate plan's crash steps (cairn-m0-e0s.11) and this bead's tests, never from `run`: on the committed 60-bit curve at the planted ceiling `8M` the real backend overflows (rc 0, EMPTY stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr — PROVEN by probe 2026-08-21), and at the bundle's `64M` it prints OK (the must-PASS control proving the entry is a live computation). `verify()` itself is NOT a crash fixture at any ceiling that starts gp: it never calls `ellcard` and prints OK on the 60-bit instance under `-s 3M`, `-s 8M` and `-s 64M` (probed 2026-08-21); below ≈ 3 MB (`-s 2M`, `-s 1M`) gp dies at startup with rc 1, stdout `### Errors on startup, exiting...` and the overflow message on stderr. The script is a gate-bundle object (kind `verifier_script`, cairn-m0-e0s.10): the driver materializes the bundle's bytes once per process to a 0444 file under `var/bundle-cache/<bundle-hash>/verify.gp` and passes that path to gp; `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp` is the bundle source and is never read at gate time.
- Driver `Verifier.run(instance: Instance, x: int) -> VerifierResult`: validates arity (exactly 9 fields), every field a non-negative int, `p > 3` (PARI's `ellinit([a,b],2)` returns `[]` and the next call dies with a fatal error at rc 0 — probed 2026-08-21; short Weierstrass is singular in characteristic 2, and the validator never lets the backend see it), `0 ≤ a, b < p`, `Px,Py,Qx,Qy < p`, `x < n`, `n` inside the Hasse interval of p (`|n − (p+1)| ≤ 2√p`) — BEFORE spawning; `Instance` reduces `a, b, Px, Py, Qx, Qy` into `[0, p)` at construction (corpus case 1's upstream `a = -3` becomes 2; cairn-m0-e0s.7) and `instance_hash` is over the reduced values; renders the nine values as decimal integer strings on ONE stdin line `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)` (never hex, never floats); spawns `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",stack_ceiling]` loading `verify.gp` through `cairn.pari.run_gp`; backend path, stack ceiling, timeout and accept predicate come from the gate bundle (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; injected as a config object at unit level) — the accept predicate is the structured object `{rc: 0, stdout: "OK", stderr_empty: true}` evaluated field by field (no string evaluation; the shipped bundle pins exactly that triple and cairn-m0-e0s.10 asserts it; `stdout: null` or `stderr_empty: false` is a legal, weaker predicate that leaves that field unchecked — the form cairn-m0-e0s.11's re-pinned bundle copy uses to prove the crash self-test is load-bearing — and only a missing key or a non-int `rc` is refused at construction); accepts iff `rc==0 AND stdout.strip()=="OK" AND stderr==""` (satisfiable — probed 2026-08-21: `gp -q -f -s 64M verify.gp` fed one stdin line writes 0 bytes to stderr on a good instance; `quit(1)` gives rc 1 with the FAIL line on stdout and empty stderr; the 8 MB stack overflow gives rc 0, empty stdout and `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr); everything else → FAIL with `reason ∈ {p-not-prime, singular, P-off-curve, Q-off-curve, nQ-not-O, xP-ne-Q, backend-crash, timeout, bad-arity, bad-field, submitter-named-instance}`: a stdout line starting with `FAIL ` yields its reason codes; every other non-accepting outcome is `backend-crash` (a fatal message on stderr with rc 0, the `-s 2M` startup overflow with rc 1 and `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout, a killed child with rc < 0, and `OK` accompanied by any stderr bytes); - Instance binding: `Instance{p,a,b,n,P,Q}` has `instance_hash = H('cairn/instance/v1' ‖ canonical instance)` (domain tag from cairn-m0-e0s.3); `run` takes an `Instance` produced by the gate run (from the claim statement node / dispatch record) and a bare `x`; a `Submission` carrying its own `(P,Q)` is refused with `reason='submitter-named-instance'` before any subprocess is spawned (a spy asserts zero spawns). The result records `instance_hash`.
- Result node: a `nodes` row of kind `verifier_result` `{instance_hash, x, accepted, reason, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, rc, wall_s}` plus a `gate_runs` row (gate='verifier', result pass|fail, instance_hash, bundle + pin hash), both written by the caller's writer (bead m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5); a verifier run is a gate run, not a skill attempt — it writes no `attempts` row and is never served from any cache (every submission re-runs the subprocess). Every verdict logs (instance_hash, accepted, reason, rc, wall_ms) at INFO and the gp argv + stdin/stdout/stderr digests at DEBUG through `cairn.log`.

title: M0: skill runner: subprocess launch with content-addressed inputs, harness-written execution receipt (CPU/wall/RSS/scratch bytes/exit/digests/bundle hash), attempt row + statuses, cache bits, 4× wall ceiling on the trivial fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §3, §5): the execution receipt is the harness's own record of the run, written by the writer and never by the skill; its readers are the budget ceiling, the ladder's clock and memory measurements and the provenance check. A receipt the skill writes about itself is a number from the gated party. Workers are subprocesses that return artifacts to the single writer and hold no write capability.

WHAT (`src/cairn/runner.py`)
- `launch(skill_module, skill_identity, inputs, seed, *, bundle_hash, scratch_dir, declared_expectation_s, declared_verification_s, budget_remaining, ceiling_multiplier) -> Attempt` (`skill_module` is the dotted module launched with `-m`, e.g. `cairn.skills.toy_curve`; `declared_expectation_s` for the toy-curve launch is `CostProfile.evaluate(bits).expected_wall_s` — the mean subprocess wall with interpreter start included, cairn-m0-e0s.6 — so the 4× ceiling is not tripped by process start): computes the recipe key (bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3); honors cache bits (`skip_cache_lookup`, `do_not_cache`, serve path of bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4); inserts the attempt row with status `RUNNING` (cairn-m0-e0s.4); spawns the skill as a subprocess (`[sys.executable, "-m", "cairn.skills.<name>"]`, canonical JSON in on stdin, canonical JSON out on stdout, scratch path passed as an argument; the child receives NO substrate path or handle and an environment scrubbed of `CAIRN_DB*`; the child's stdout and stderr go to files `<attempt dir>/stdout` and `<attempt dir>/stderr` outside the scratch path whose byte delta is measured — never pipes, and `communicate()` is never called, because it reaps the child through `wait()` (subprocess.py 1212/1239/2152, CPython 3.14.0 under uv; probed by cairn-m0-e0s.2 probe 7) — so `os.wait4` is the first and only reap and the stdout/stderr digests are BLAKE3 over those two files); waits with `os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)` for rusage (ru_utime, ru_stime, ru_maxrss) and takes the exit status from the status word it returns (`os.waitstatus_to_exitcode`), setting `proc.returncode` itself and never calling `proc.wait()`/`proc.poll()` afterwards — CPython's `Popen._try_wait` turns the `ChildProcessError` of an already-reaped child into status 0 (subprocess.py, read 2026-08-21 on Python 3.14.3), which would record every crash as exit 0; `time.monotonic()` start/end; wall; bytes written under scratch (directory-size delta); exit status; stdout/stderr BLAKE3 digests; tool digests (gp sha256, cypari2/libpari versions); bundle hash. Writes the receipt node and closes the attempt row (the single RUNNING→terminal UPDATE) with status: `OK` (exit 0, well-formed output, skill status OK); `FAIL` (non-zero exit, malformed output, or skill status FAIL); `DISAGREE` (skill status DISAGREE); `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (wall past `ceiling = multiplier × declared_expectation_s`, the `ceiling_multiplier` argument, which the caller reads from the opened bundle's `tiers.ceiling_multiplier` — 4 at M0, CONJECTURE, §5; cairn-m0-e0s.10 — the runner never opens the bundle itself: the e2e slice (cairn-m0-e0s.14) passes it from the bundle and the tests pass 4 → child killed). `startup_scan()` moves every `RUNNING` attempt with NULL `ended_at` to `INTERRUPTED` before any new launch (M0 implements the scan; M3 exercises it under crash tests).
- Output manifest: each artifact a blob (hash,size); the manifest node (kind `output_manifest`, `{attempt_id, artifacts: sorted map name → (hash,size)}`) is linked by `lineage` rows child → parent: `manifest → recipe_key` (`edge_kind='output_of'`), `manifest → each input blob` (`'input'`) and `each output blob → manifest` (`'member'`); the attempt row (`attempt_id` is not a content hash) is reached through `attempts.recipe_key` and `attempts.output_manifest_hash`, never through `lineage` — the edge set GC's reachability walks (cairn-m0-e0s.13).
- Escrow: writes the reservation columns at launch — `declared_production_cost = declared_expectation_s`, `declared_verification_cost = declared_verification_s` (the toy-curve launch passes `Evaluation.expected_core_s` and `.expected_verification_core_s`, cairn-m0-e0s.6), `reserved = declared_verification_cost`, `ceiling_multiplier`, `spent_at`/`released_at` NULL (schema-only at M0; reserve/spend/release behavior is M1).
- Logging: each launch logs (recipe key, served-from-cache | spawned, argv at DEBUG, status, wall_ms, cpu_s, rss) through `cairn.log`; a kill logs the ceiling and the elapsed wall.
TESTS (integration, `tests/integration/test_runner.py`; the launch subject is the real `toy_curve` skill, cairn-m0-e0s.6): launch toy_curve 40-bit seed 1 → attempt OK; receipt has cpu>0, wall>0, rss>0, stdout_digest == BLAKE3 of captured stdout; output manifest hash equals the skill's own manifest; second identical launch → served from cache, no new attempt; with `skip_cache_lookup` → new attempt, same manifest (Replayable double-attempt agreement); fixture skill exiting 3 → FAIL attempt, never served, and its receipt's `exit_status == 3` (a status read through Popen after the wait4 reap would be 0); fixture sleeping 2 s with declared expectation 0.2 s → killed at 0.8 s, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, never served, its receipt's `exit_status` carrying the kill signal; fixture emitting a `receipt` key in its output → ignored (receipt.cpu differs from the fake); fixture that prints its environment → no substrate path visible; fixture writing 1 MB to stderr then exiting 0 → attempt OK with no deadlock and `stderr_digest` equal to BLAKE3 of the captured file; fixture skills live in `tests/fixtures/skills/` (`exit3.py`, `sleep2.py`, `fake_receipt.py`, `print_env.py`, `stderr_1mb.py`) and are launched by module path with `tests/fixtures` on the child's `PYTHONPATH`, set by the test; `startup_scan()` on a DB with an unfinished RUNNING attempt marks it INTERRUPTED and a later `serve` ignores it.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_runner_status.py`, no subprocess): the status mapping table (exit, stdout well-formedness, skill status, wall vs ceiling) → exactly one of OK/FAIL/DISAGREE/BUDGET_EXCEEDED; ceiling arithmetic (`4 × 0.2 s = 0.8 s`); the environment scrub removes every `CAIRN_DB*` variable.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Fuzzing (`tests/unit/test_runner_fuzz.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500, no subprocess): the pure skill-stdout parser `parse_skill_output(stdout_bytes) -> ParsedOutput | Malformed(reason)` over `st.binary()`, arbitrary JSON from `st.recursive(...)`, a valid-shaped object with wrong field types, truncated canonical JSON (a valid document cut at `st.integers(0, len)`), a `receipt` key, `status` outside `OK | FAIL | DISAGREE`, `NaN`/`Infinity` tokens, nesting depth 200, a 1 MB payload, two concatenated documents, a UTF-8 BOM, trailing garbage — never raises; every malformed input maps to attempt status `FAIL` (`status_for(parsed, exit, wall, ceiling)` yields `FAIL`) unless stdout is exactly one canonical-JSON object with the declared fields and a `status` in the vocabulary; the `receipt` key is ignored on every input; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/runner_mutants.py`: `parser_json_loads_bare` (propagates `JSONDecodeError`), `status_default_ok` (missing `status` → OK), `receipt_trusted` (copies a child-supplied `receipt`) — each killed; seed corpus `tests/fuzz_corpus/runner/` with those negatives replayed as `@example`s.
- Failure-path convergence: the status mapping is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over the full table `(exit ∈ {0, 3, -9}, well_formed ∈ {yes, no}, skill_status ∈ {OK, FAIL, DISAGREE, missing}, wall_vs_ceiling ∈ {under, over})` → exactly one of `OK | FAIL | DISAGREE | BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `ids=` naming the cell; the five fixture-skill integration cases stay separate (each exercises a different real child).
- Every runner integration test calls `db_snapshot` after launch (attempts, receipts, blobs, lineage counts) so a double-written attempt shows in the log.
- Conformance: the launch contract this runner enforces (canonical JSON on stdin/stdout, no substrate handle, scrubbed environment, module entry point) is checked per skill by the §2 harness (cairn-m0-e0s.16) through this runner — the runner's own tests assert the runner, the harness asserts each skill.

description:

DONE WHEN: a parked branch auto-revives on blocker-clear; a refuted hypothesis key is `Blocked` unaided; a proposal whose declared region contains a measured REFUTED point for the same method and cost model is `Blocked` though its key is fresh; a `supersedes` edge into a REFUTED version with an unmet retry predicate parks with `supersedes_refuted_review` until the attributed difference statement is recorded; a refutation without a null arm parks the proposal with `null_control_pending`, the blocker clears when the re-measurement lands, and the preflight then answers `Allowed` — with the table as the evidence that met the retry predicate — when the re-measurement did not REJECT and `Blocked` when it did; a proposal differing from a `measured` REFUTED entry only in implementation revision is `Blocked`, while one differing from an `implementation` entry by a certified new revision is `Allowed`; a new branch opened on a key a promoted branch holds — or whose claim statement stands at STRONG-EMPIRICAL after the branch that earned it withdrew — or on a sub-region of such a holder's region with the same method identity and cost model, parks with `already_settled` until a superseding object with its difference statement is recorded; a log truncated to an earlier valid prefix fails startup verification against the checkpoint — also when the truncated log has been re-extended and its forked head appended to the checkpoint, since every older checkpointed head must remain a prefix head (§3) — and an unreachable checkpoint blocks promotion; a worker that returns with a claim it opened still open yields a `Leaked` record while a harness-terminated attempt yields none; and a green Lean artifact with no `review_verdict` stays below PROVEN while the statement-review workflow routes it to the human queue.

ADDS: the ledger preflight (`Allowed | Blocked | RequiresNullControl | AlreadySettled`) with its measured-point reach, `supersedes_refuted_review`, `null_control_pending` and `already_settled` parks with the null-control resolution rule, the hash-chained log (`chain = H(domain ‖ prior_chain ‖ canonical_record)`) and its head checkpoint (a file beside the gate-bundle pin carrying the append-only flag — M0 grounded what that flag refuses; the second OS user arrives at M3 per decision 8), the terminal-status invariant, the statement-review workflow routing green artifacts to the human queue and recording `review_verdict` nodes through the human path, and the near-duplicate advisory (64-bit SimHash over hypothesis text; advisory only) routed to the human or to a `near_dup_review` park (Librarian routing arrives at M4).

description:
SCOPE (PLAN §13 M3): Branch tree + bandit + info-per-dollar allocation + structured self-redesign (data, not gates). Decompose when M2 closes. The orchestrator may rewrite the branch tree, funding and prompts — never the gates, calibration taxonomy, ladder, verifier, no-go checklist, or what counts as proven (CLAUDE.md). Operator decision 8: the separate OS user for the orchestrator process arrives here (the pin and attestation file then bind by ownership, not only by mode); decision 3: Tier-2 spend no longer requires an open operator session once the orchestrator exists — revisit then.

- ≥20 seeded runs with the named outcomes; `k`, `m` pinned in the test plan; the orchestrator's path writes no REFUTED row and no withdrawn status in any run (asserted by query).
